\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu}=\mu\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\equiv\mu_{X}\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{P}\,{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-1.0ptX\longrightarrow M

and right action

(4.9)

\displaystyle\widetilde{\varrho}\hskip-2.0pt:(\mathscr{P}\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\widetilde{\mu}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{t}\hskip-2.0pt\mathscr{G}\longrightarrow\mathscr{P}\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\,,\ \bigl((p,x),g\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl(\varrho(p,g),\lambda_{X}\bigl(g^{-1},x\bigr)\bigr)\,.

The above implies a canonical identification

\displaystyle\Xi\cong(\mathscr{P}\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)/\mathscr{G}

Proof.

Consider smooth local maps

(4.10)

\displaystyle\qquad\delta_{X\,i}\hskip-2.0pt:\pi_{\mathscr{P}}^{-1}(O_{i})\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\longrightarrow\Xi,\ \bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g),x\bigr)\longmapsto[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g,x),i)]\,,\quad i\in I\,,

written in the convenient model (
4.5
) of
\Xi
. At an arbitrary point
\sigma^{\prime}\in O_{ij}
, we find

(4.12)

\displaystyle\delta_{X\,i}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{j}^{-1}(\sigma^{\prime},g),x\bigr)=\delta_{X\,i}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma^{\prime},\beta_{ij}(\sigma^{\prime})\vartriangleright g\bigr),x\bigr)\equiv[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(\beta_{ij}(\sigma^{\prime})\vartriangleright g,x),i)]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle[(\sigma,(\lambda_{X}((\beta_{ij}(\sigma^{\prime}))(t(g)),\lambda_{X}(g,x)),i)]\equiv[(\sigma,(\lambda_{X}((\beta_{ij}(\sigma^{\prime}))(\mu_{X}(\lambda_{X}(g,x))),\lambda_{X}(g,x)),i)]

(4.14)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle[(\sigma,B\lambda_{X}(\beta_{ij}(\sigma^{\prime}),\lambda_{X}(g,x)),i)]=[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g,x),j)]\equiv\delta_{X\,j}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{j}^{-1}(\sigma^{\prime},g),x\bigr)\,,

meaning that the
\delta_{X\,i}
are restrictions of a globally smooth map

\displaystyle\delta_{X}\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\longrightarrow\Xi\,,\qquad\delta_{X}\big|_{\pi_{\mathscr{P}}^{-1}(O_{i})\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\ }\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX}=\delta_{X\,i}\,.

In the next step, we check, for arbitrary
\sigma\in O_{i},\ (g,h)\in\mathscr{G}\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{t}\hskip-2.0pt\mathscr{G}
and
x\in\mu_{X}^{-1}(\{s(g)\}))
, the identity

(4.16)

\displaystyle\bigl(\delta_{X}\circ\widetilde{\varrho}_{h}\bigr)\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g),x\bigr)\equiv\delta_{X}\bigl(\varrho\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g),h\bigr),\lambda_{X}\bigl(h^{-1},x\bigr)\bigr)=\delta_{X}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g.h),\lambda_{X}\bigl(h^{-1},x\bigr)\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g.h,\lambda_{X}(h^{-1},x)))]=[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g.h.h^{-1},x))]=[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g,x))]\equiv\delta_{X}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g),x\bigr)\,,

which implies that
({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\varrho})
maps as

\displaystyle({\rm pr}_{1,2},\widetilde{\varrho})\hskip-2.0pt:(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\widetilde{\mu}\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{t}\hskip-2.0pt\mathscr{G}\longrightarrow(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\delta_{X}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\delta_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)

At this stage, it suffices to prove the existence of a (smooth) division map

\displaystyle\widetilde{\phi}\hskip-2.0pt:(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\delta_{X}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\delta_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\longrightarrow\mathscr{G}

with the property
({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\phi})=({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\varrho})^{-1}
. As
\delta_{X}
is a vertical bundle map, we may define the map sought after as

\displaystyle\widetilde{\phi}:=\phi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1,3}

in terms of the division map
\phi_{\mathscr{P}}
of
\mathscr{P}
. We readily verify, for
((p,x),g)\in(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\widetilde{\mu}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{t}\hskip-2.0pt\mathscr{G}
,

\displaystyle\bigl(({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\phi})\circ({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\varrho})\bigr)\bigl((p,x),g\bigr)\equiv({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\phi})\bigl((p,x),\bigl(\varrho(p,g),\lambda_{X}\bigl(g^{-1},x\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)\equiv\bigl((p,x),\phi_{\mathscr{P}}\bigl(p,\varrho(p,g)\bigr)\bigr)=\bigl((p,x),g\bigr)\,,

and, for
((p_{1},x_{1}),(p_{2},x_{2}))\in(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\ }\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt\,X)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\delta_{X}\ }\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\delta_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt\,(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\ }\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt\,X)
such that
(p_{a},x_{a})=(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g_{a}),x_{a}),

a\in\{1,2\}
,

(4.18)

\displaystyle\bigl(({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\varrho})\circ({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\phi})\bigr)\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),(p_{2},x_{2})\bigr)\equiv({\rm pr}_{1},\widetilde{\varrho})\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),\phi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),\widetilde{\varrho}\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),\phi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})\bigr)\bigr)=\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),\bigl(\varrho\bigl(p_{1},\phi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})\bigr),\lambda_{X}\bigl(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})^{-1},x_{1}\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)

(4.20)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),\bigl(p_{2},\lambda_{X}\bigl(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})^{-1},x_{1}\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)=\bigl((p_{1},x_{1}),(p_{2},x_{2})\bigr)\,,

where the last equality follows from

\displaystyle[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g_{1},x_{1}),i)]\equiv\delta_{X}(p_{1},x_{1})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{=}}\delta_{X}(p_{2},x_{2})\equiv[(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g_{2},x_{2}),i)]\,,

the latter implying

\displaystyle\lambda_{X}\bigl(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})^{-1},x_{1}\bigr)=\lambda_{X}\bigl((g_{1}^{-1}.g_{2})^{-1},x_{1}\bigr)=\lambda_{X}\bigl(g_{2}^{-1}.g_{1},x_{1}\bigr)=x_{2}\,.

∎

Definition 4.5
.

Adopt the notation of Thm.
4.4
. We shall call the fibre bundle
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\Sigma,\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s\,\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1})
a
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
, and the fibre bundle
(\Xi,\Sigma,X,\pi_{\Xi})
a
bundle associated to

\mathscr{P}

by
\lambda_{X}
, or a
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle
for short. The map
\lambda_{X}
shall be termed, in this context, the
associating
\mathscr{G}
-action
, and the map
\delta_{X}
the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient map
.

We may readily reinterpret the construction of the associated bundle
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)/\mathscr{G}
as a distinguished specialisation of the construction of the shadow bundle of a principaloid bundle with the structure groupoid given by the action groupoid
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
from Prop.
B.25
. The specialisation hinges upon

Proposition 4.6
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
B.7
and
B.20
, and of Prop.
B.25
. Let
(X,\mu_{X},\lambda_{X})
be a left
\mathscr{G}
-module. The moment map
\mu_{X}\hskip-2.0pt:X\to M
canonically induces a group homomorphism

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}=\bigl(\mu_{X}^{*}(\cdot),{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm Bisec}\bigl(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt\bigr)\longrightarrow{\rm Bisec}\bigl(\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X\bigr),\ \beta\longmapsto\bigl(\beta\circ\mu_{X},{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)\,.

Whenever
\mu_{X}
is surjective, the homomorphism is injective.

Proof.

Consider an arbitrary bisection
\beta\in{\rm Bisec}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)
. We then have

\displaystyle\widetilde{s}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)\equiv{\rm pr}_{2}\circ\bigl(\beta\circ\mu_{X},{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)={\rm id}_{X}\,,

and so, indeed,
\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)
is a section of the surjective submersion
\widetilde{s}
. In order to verify that its manifestly smooth post-composition with
\widetilde{t}
,

\displaystyle\widetilde{t}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)\equiv\lambda_{X}\circ\bigl(\beta\circ\mu_{X},{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)\,,

yields a diffeomorphism of
X
, we check directly that another smooth map:

\displaystyle\widetilde{t}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}\bigl(\beta^{-1}\bigr)\equiv\lambda_{X}\circ\bigl({\rm Inv}\circ\beta\circ(t_{*}\beta)^{-1}\circ\mu_{X},{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)

is the inverse of
\widetilde{t}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)
,

\displaystyle\widetilde{t}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}\bigl(\beta^{-1}\bigr)=\bigl(\widetilde{t}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)\bigr)^{-1}\,.

Hence,

\displaystyle\widetilde{t}\circ\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)\in{\rm Diff}(X)\,,

and, consequently,

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}(\beta)\in{\rm Bisec}\bigl(\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X\bigr)\,,

as desired. The homomorphicity of
\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}
is readily verified.

Finally, the injectivity of
\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}
in the case of a surjective moment map
\mu_{X}
is obvious.
∎

With the last result in hand, we may state the anticipated

Proposition 4.7
.

Adopt the notation of Prop.
4.6
and Thms.
3.3
and
4.4
. The fibre bundle
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\Sigma,\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s\,\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1})
is a principaloid
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-bundle with the structure group reduced to
L({\rm Im}\,\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*})\subset L({\rm Bisec}(\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X))
. The fibre bundle
(\Xi,\Sigma,X,\pi_{\Xi})
associated to
\mathscr{P}
by
\lambda_{X}
is the corresponding shadow bundle, and the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient map

is the sitting-duck map between the two. This is captured by the diagram

(4.21)

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern written for the moment map

\displaystyle\widehat{\mu}{}_{X}={\rm pr}_{2}\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\longrightarrow X\,,

and for the action map

(4.23)

\displaystyle\widehat{\varrho}{}_{X}=\widetilde{\varrho}\circ{\rm pr}_{1,2,3}

\displaystyle\hskip-2.0pt:

\displaystyle(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\widehat{\mu}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\lambda_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt(\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\longrightarrow\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX

\displaystyle\hskip-2.0pt:

\displaystyle\bigl((p,x),\bigl(g,\lambda_{X}\bigl(g^{-1},x\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl(\varrho(p,g),\lambda_{X}\bigl(g^{-1},x\bigr)\bigr)\,.

Proof.

The model (
3.2
) of
\mathscr{P}
gives us a convenient presentation of the bundle of interest:

\displaystyle\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\cong\bigsqcup_{i\in I}\,\bigl(O_{i}\times\bigl(\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\bigr)/\sim_{\widetilde{L}{}_{\beta_{\cdot\cdot}}}\,,

in which the identification of fibres over
O_{ij}\ni\sigma
is realised by the diffeomorphisms

\displaystyle(\sigma,g,x,j)\sim\bigl(\sigma,\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\vartriangleright g,x,i\bigr)\,,

consistently with the fibration over
M
,

\displaystyle s\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\vartriangleright g\bigr)=s(g)=\mu_{X}(x)\,.

The diffeomorphisms can be rewritten as

(4.25)

\displaystyle\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\vartriangleright g,x\bigr)\equiv\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigl(t(g)\bigr).g,x\bigr)\equiv\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigl(t(g)\bigr),\lambda_{X}(g,x)\bigr).(g,x)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigl(\bigl(\mu_{X}\circ\lambda_{X}\bigr)(g,x)\bigr),\lambda_{X}(g,x)\bigr).(g,x)\equiv\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)\bigl(\widetilde{t}(g,x)\bigr).(g,x)\equiv\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)\vartriangleright(g,x)\,,

and so we arrive at

\displaystyle\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\cong\bigsqcup_{i\in I}\,\bigl(O_{i}\times\bigl(\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\bigr)/\sim_{L_{\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}\circ\beta_{\cdot\cdot}}}\,.

The identification of the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient (bundle) map
\delta_{X}\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\to\Xi
as the principal
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-bundle now follows from the local formulæ (
4.10
), from which the desired local model
\lambda_{X}\equiv\widetilde{t}
of the map emerges. Equivalently, we note that, for
\sigma\in O_{ij}
and
x\in X
,

\displaystyle\widetilde{t}{}_{*}\bigl(\bigl(\widetilde{\mu}{}_{X}^{*}\circ\beta_{ij}\bigr)(\sigma)\bigr)(x)=\bigl(\lambda_{X}\circ\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\circ\mu_{X},{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)\bigr)(x)=\lambda_{X}\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigl(\mu_{X}(x)\bigr),x\bigr)\equiv B\lambda_{X}\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma),x\bigr)\,.

The remaining statements of the proposition are straightforward.
∎

The two principal groupoid-bundle structures on
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\Xi,\delta_{X})
discussed above are related by the Lie-groupoid morphism of Prop.

between the two structure groupoids, as captured by the commutative diagram

{\rm{\bf Gr}}\equiv\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
).

Proof.

First of all, we need to check the global smoothness of
\Upsilon_{X}
as defined (locally) in (
4.27
). To this end, consider
\sigma\in O_{ij}
and calculate

(4.29)

\displaystyle\Upsilon_{X}\bigl(\Xi\tau_{j}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,B\lambda_{X}\bigl(\beta_{ji}(\sigma),x\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)\equiv\Upsilon_{X}\bigl(\Xi\tau_{j}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,\lambda_{X}\bigl(\beta_{ji}(\sigma)\bigl(\mu_{X}(x)\bigr),x\bigr)\bigr)\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\mathscr{F}\tau_{j}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,\mu_{X}\bigl(\lambda_{X}\bigl(\beta_{ji}(\sigma)\bigl(\mu_{X}(x)\bigr),x\bigr)\bigr)=\mathscr{F}\tau_{j}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,t_{*}\bigl(\beta_{ji}(\sigma)\bigr)\bigl(\mu_{X}(x)\bigr)\bigr)=\mathscr{F}\tau_{i}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,\mu_{X}(x)\bigr)\equiv\Upsilon_{X}\bigl(\Xi\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,x)\bigr)\,.

Having verified the well-definedness of
\Upsilon_{X}
, we may, next, inspect diagram (
4.26
). Thus, at an arbitrary point
(p,x)\in\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
with
p=\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g)
, we obtain

(4.31)

\displaystyle(\mathscr{D}\circ{\rm pr}_{1})(p,x)=\mathscr{D}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g)\bigr)=\mathscr{F}\tau_{i}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,t(g)\bigr)\equiv\mathscr{F}\tau_{i}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,\bigl(\mu_{X}\circ\lambda_{X}\bigr)(g,x)\bigr)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\Upsilon_{X}\bigl(\Xi\tau_{i}^{-1}\bigl(\sigma,\lambda_{X}(g,x)\bigr)\bigr)\equiv\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\delta_{X}\bigr)\bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g),x\bigr)\equiv\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\delta_{X}\bigr)(p,x)\,,

which establishes the stated commutativity of the diagram.

That the fibres of the respective moment maps are preserved by the above morphism follows from the tautological commutativity of the diagram

4.2.
Associated gauge transformations

In the next step, we study another manifestation of the reduction of the structure group through association, to wit: the reduction of the gauge group of the associated principaloid bundle. As anticipated, the reduction is encoded in the action of the Ehresmann–Atiyah groupoid of the underlying principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}
.

Theorem 4.11
.

Adopt the notation of Prop.
4.8
and Thm.
3.8
. The Ehresmann–Atiyah groupoid
{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})
of a principaloid
\mathscr{G}
-bundle
\mathscr{P}
acts on the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX

\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle

\bullet

\mu_{X}
-extended bundle

-module, with moment map

and action

(4.32)

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}=\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}\times{\rm id}_{X}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{{\mathsf{S}}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\widetilde{\mu}{}_{\mathscr{P}}}\hskip-2.0pt(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\longrightarrow\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\ \bigl(a,(p,x)\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl(\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}(a,p),x\bigr)\,,

and action

\displaystyle\lambda_{\Sigma}\hskip-2.0pt:(\Sigma\times\Sigma)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{{\rm pr}_{2}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{{\rm id}_{\Sigma}}\hskip-2.0pt\Sigma\longrightarrow\Sigma,\ \bigl((\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2}),\sigma_{2}\bigr)\longmapsto\sigma_{1}\,.

by the

-quotient map

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu}{}_{\mathscr{P}}=\mu_{\Xi}\circ\delta_{X}\,,\qquad\qquad\lambda_{\Xi}\circ\bigl({\rm id}_{{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})}\times\delta_{X}\bigr)=\delta_{X}\circ\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}\,.

Proof.

A trivial direct check.

Proof.

The commutativity of the extended
W
-diagram inscribed into the trident follows directly from the very definition of the fibred product
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
and from Prop.
4.8
, see Diag.
4.26
. It identifies
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\Xi,\delta_{X},\mu_{X}\circ{\rm pr}_{2},\widetilde{\varrho})
as the (right) principal
\mathscr{G}
-bundle described in Thm.
4.4
.

Next, we consider the left
{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})
-module
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,X,\Upsilon_{X}\circ\delta_{X}\equiv\widetilde{\mu}{}_{\mathscr{P}},\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}})
of Thm.
4.11
, the form of the moment map following, once more, from the commutativity of the diagram above. The action
\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}
trivially preserves
{\rm pr}_{2}
-fibres, see (
4.32
), and so we have a well-defined map

\displaystyle\bigl(\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}},{\rm pr}_{2,3}\bigr)\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{{\mathsf{S}}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\widetilde{\mu}{}_{\mathscr{P}}}\hskip-2.0pt\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\longrightarrow\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{{\rm pr}_{2}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{{\rm pr}_{2}}\hskip-2.0pt\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\,.

Define a (smooth) map

\displaystyle\widetilde{\psi}{}_{\mathscr{P}}:=\psi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1,3}\hskip-2.0pt:\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{{\rm pr}_{2}}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{{\rm pr}_{2}}\hskip-2.0pt\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\longrightarrow{\rm At}(\mathscr{P}),\ \bigl((p_{1},x),(p_{2},x)\bigr)\longmapsto\psi_{\mathscr{P}}(p_{1},p_{2})\,,

taking into account the identity
\mu(p_{2})=\mu_{X}(x)=\mu(p_{1})
, and then invoking Thm.
3.6
(see: (
3.27
)). This is readily verified to be the division map for
\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}
. Thus, the principality of
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,X,{\rm pr}_{2},\Upsilon_{X}\circ\delta_{X},\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}})
is established, whence, in particular, the canonical identification

\displaystyle X\cong\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)/{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})

ensues by the Godement Criterion, see: Thm.
A.5
.

We may, now, investigate properties of the two associating actions:
\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}
and
\widetilde{\varrho}
relative to each other, to the principal projection
{\rm pr}_{1}
, and to the respective extending moment maps
\delta_{X}
and
{\rm pr}_{2}
. We start by noting that the two associating actions commute because so do the underlying actions
\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}
and
\varrho
on
\mathscr{P}
. Moreover, the first component in each pair of chiral actions:
(\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}},\lambda_{\mathscr{P}})
and
(\widetilde{\varrho},\varrho)
being a lift of the second one along
{\rm pr}_{1}
, the latter map automatically intertwines the two components. Finally, we note that
\delta_{X}
is
{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})
-equivariant by definition, and, likewise,
{\rm pr}_{2}
intertwines
\widetilde{\varrho}
with
\varrho_{X}\equiv\lambda_{X}\circ({\rm Inv}\circ{\rm pr}_{2},{\rm pr}_{1})
, see (
4.9
). Thus, by now, we have the structure of an
({\rm At}(\mathscr{P}),\mathscr{G})
-bibundle
(\lambda_{\Xi},\varrho_{X})
-associated to the principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}
established on the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
, and captured neatly by the extended
W
-diagram

That the left wing of the above diagram fibres as claimed over the pair groupoid
{\rm Pair}(\Sigma)
of the common base
\Sigma
of the bundles
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\Xi,\mathscr{P}
and
\mathscr{F}
follows directly from the definitions of the four bundles, put in conjunction with the fact that all these maps are
\Sigma
-vertical,
i.e.
, they are morphisms in the slice category
{\rm{\bf Bun}}(\Sigma)/\Sigma
.
∎

The induction of the structure of an
{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})
-module space on the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
and its descent to the quotient
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)/\mathscr{G}\cong\Xi
pave the way to the introduction of distinguished automorphisms of the
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle
\Xi
, including its gauge transformations.

Proposition 4.13
.

Adopt the notation of Props.
3.13
and
4.8
. There exist canonical group homomorphisms

\displaystyle{\rm Ext}_{X}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm Aut}(\mathscr{P})\longrightarrow{\rm Aut}\bigl(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\,,\qquad\qquad\Xi_{*}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm Aut}(\mathscr{P})\longrightarrow{\rm Aut}(\Xi)\,,

where
{\rm Aut}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)
is the group of automorphisms of the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
as a principaloid
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-bundle (see: Prop.
4.7
), whereas
{\rm Aut}(\Xi)
is the group of automorphisms of
\Xi
as a fibre bundle. These homomorphisms satisfy, for all
\Phi\in{\rm Aut}(\mathscr{P})
, the equivariance identities

(4.35)

\displaystyle\delta_{X}\circ{\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)=\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\circ\delta_{X}\,,

(4.36)

(4.37)

\displaystyle\Upsilon_{X}\circ\Xi_{*}(\Phi)=\mathscr{F}_{*}(\Phi)\circ\Upsilon_{X}\,.

Proof.

The existence of
{\rm Ext}_{X}
and
\Xi_{*}
is ensured by Thm.
3.16
and Prop.
B.27
. When put in conjunction, these yield, for
\Phi\in{\rm Aut}(\mathscr{P})
arbitrary and all
(p,x)\in\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
,

(4.39)

\displaystyle{\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)(p,x)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle B\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}\bigl(\beta_{\Phi},(p,x)\bigr)\equiv\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\bigl(\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\delta_{X}\bigr)(p,x)\bigr),(p,x)\bigr)=\bigl(\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}\times{\rm id}_{X}\bigr)\bigl(\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\circ\mathscr{D}\bigr)(p)\bigr),(p,x)\bigr)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\bigl(\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}\bigl(\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\circ\mu_{\mathscr{P}}\bigr)(p),p\bigr),x\bigr)=\bigl(\Phi(p),x\bigr)\,,

where the third and last equalities use the commutativity of Diags. (
4.26
) and (
3.32
), respectively, and, for all
\xi\in\Xi
,

\displaystyle\Xi_{*}(\Phi)(\xi)=B\lambda_{\Xi}(\beta_{\Phi},\xi)\equiv\lambda_{\Xi}\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}(\xi)\bigr),\xi\bigr)\,.

Hence, we may write

\displaystyle{\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)=\Phi\times{\rm id}_{X}\,,

and

\displaystyle\Xi_{*}(\Phi)=\lambda_{\Xi}\circ(\beta_{\Phi}\circ\Upsilon_{X},{\rm id}_{\Xi})\,.

It is, in particular, clear that the
\varrho
-equivariance of
\Phi
ensures the
\widetilde{\varrho}
-equivariance of the induced bundle automorphism
{\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)
.

Identity (
4.35
) now follows from a direct calculation, invoking the second of identities (
4.34
) and, once more, Diags. (
4.26
) and (
3.32
),

(4.41)

\displaystyle\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\circ\delta_{X}\bigr)(p,x)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lambda_{\Xi}\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\bigl(\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\delta_{X}\bigr)(p,x)\bigr),\delta_{X}(p,x)\bigr)\equiv\bigl(\lambda_{\Xi}\circ\bigl({\rm id}_{{\rm At}(\mathscr{P})}\times\delta_{X}\bigr)\bigr)\bigl(\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\circ\mathscr{D}\bigr)(p),(p,x)\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl(\delta_{X}\circ\widetilde{\lambda}{}_{\mathscr{P}}\bigr)\bigl(\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\circ\mathscr{D}\bigr)(p),(p,x)\bigr)\equiv\delta_{X}\bigl(\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}\bigl(\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\circ\mu_{\mathscr{P}}\bigr)(p),p\bigr),x\bigr)=\delta_{X}\bigl(\Phi(p),x\bigr)\,.

Similarly, for (
4.37
), we compute, using the commutativity of Diag.
3.31
and the identification of
\Upsilon_{X}
as the moment map for the action
\lambda_{\Xi}
along the way,

\displaystyle\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)(\xi)\equiv\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\lambda_{\Xi}\bigr)\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}(\xi)\bigr),\xi\bigr)={\mathsf{T}}\bigl(\beta_{\Phi}\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}(\xi)\bigr)\bigr)\equiv\bigl({\mathsf{T}}\circ\beta_{\Phi}\bigr)\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}(\xi)\bigr)=\mathscr{F}_{*}(\Phi)\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}(\xi)\bigr)\,.

∎

.

4.3.
Induced connections on associated bundles

The last element of the associating construction is the induction of distinguished connections on the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle and on the
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle from a
\mathscr{G}
-invariant connection on the underlying principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}
. This is described in

Proposition 4.15
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
3.21
and Thm.
4.4
. Every (compatible) Ehresmann connection
{\rm T}\mathscr{P}\cong{\rm H}\mathscr{P}\oplus{\rm V}\mathscr{P}
on a principaloid
\mathscr{G}
-bundle
\mathscr{P}
canonically induces a
\mathscr{G}
-invariant, and hence—equivalently—
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-invariant Ehresmann connection on the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\Sigma,\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1})
as

\displaystyle{\rm T}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)={\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\oplus{\rm H}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,,

(4.42)

(4.43)

\displaystyle{\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm V}\mathscr{P}\,{}_{{\rm T}\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\oplus_{{\rm T}\mu_{X}}\hskip-1.0pt{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X\,,\qquad{\rm H}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm H}\mathscr{P}\,,

where the Whitney sum is
{\rm T}M
-fibred as

\displaystyle{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm V}\mathscr{P}\,{}_{{\rm T}\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\oplus_{{\rm T}\mu_{X}}\hskip-1.0pt{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X=\bigl\{\ (V,\xi)\in{\rm V}_{p}\mathscr{P}\oplus{\rm T}_{x}X\quad|\quad{\rm T}_{p}\mu(V)={\rm T}_{x}\mu_{X}(\xi)\,,\quad(p,x)\in\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\ \bigr\}\,.

Consequently,
{\rm H}\mathscr{P}
also induces—along the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient map
\delta_{X}
—a connection on the
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle
(\Xi\cong(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)/\mathscr{G},\Sigma,X,\pi_{\Xi})
as

(4.44)

\displaystyle\qquad\qquad{\rm T}\Xi={\rm V}\Xi\oplus{\rm H}\Xi\,,\qquad\qquad{\rm V}\Xi={\rm T}\delta_{X}({\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm V}\mathscr{P}\,{}_{{\rm T}\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\oplus_{{\rm T}\mu_{X}}\hskip-1.0pt{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X)\,,\qquad{\rm H}\Xi={\rm T}\delta_{X}({\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm H}\mathscr{P})\,.

Proof.

The tangent bundle of the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle can be obtained from that of the cartesian product

\displaystyle{\rm T}(\mathscr{P}\times X)\cong{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm T}\mathscr{P}\oplus{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X

by defining the relevant
{\rm T}M
-fibred subbundle
7
7

7

Note that
{\rm T}\mu\circ{\rm pr}_{1}-{\rm T}\mu_{X}\circ{\rm pr}_{2}
has maximal and hence constant rank owing to the submersivity of
\mu
.

(4.46)

\displaystyle{\rm ker}\,({\rm T}\mu\circ{\rm pr}_{1}-{\rm T}\mu_{X}\circ{\rm pr}_{2})={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm T}\mathscr{P}\,{}_{{\rm T}\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\oplus_{{\rm T}\mu_{X}}\hskip-1.0pt{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\bigl\{\ (V,\xi)\in{\rm T}_{p}\mathscr{P}\oplus{\rm T}_{x}X\quad|\quad{\rm T}_{p}\mu(V)={\rm T}_{x}\mu_{X}(\xi)\,,\quad(p,x)\in\mathscr{P}\times X\ \bigr\}

and subsequently restricting the latter to the submanifold
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\subset\mathscr{P}\times X
, whereby the tangent of that submanifold is recovered,

\displaystyle{\rm T}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0pt\hskip-1.0ptX)={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm T}\mathscr{P}\,{}_{{\rm T}\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\oplus_{{\rm T}\mu_{X}}\hskip-1.0pt{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X\,.

Taking into account Prop.
4.7
in conjunction with Def.
3.21
, we see that the horizontal distribution of a
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-invariant connection on
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
—which is the same as a
\mathscr{G}
-invariant connection on that bundle—necessarily lies in

\displaystyle{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}\widehat{\mu}{}_{X}\equiv{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}{\rm pr}_{2}={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}\mu\supset{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm H}\mathscr{P}\,.

Upon further noting that
\widehat{\varrho}
restricts to
\varrho
in the first cartesian factor in
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
, we conclude that the pullback along
{\rm pr}_{1}
of a
\mathscr{G}
-invariant distribution
{\rm H}\mathscr{P}
within
{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}\mu
is automatically
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-invariant, and so does, indeed, determine a
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-invariant connection on
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
relative to the
common
base
\Sigma
of
\mathscr{P}
and
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
.

The identification of the vertical subbundle in
{\rm T}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)
, on the other hand, follows straightforwardly from the structure of the base projection,

\displaystyle\pi_{\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX}=\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad{\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\equiv{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}(\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1})={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\,{}_{{\rm T}\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\oplus_{{\rm T}\mu^{X}}\hskip-1.0pt{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}X\,.

The last part of the proposition is now implied by Prop.
3.25
upon invoking Prop.
4.7
.
∎

Definition 4.16
.

Adopt the notation of Prop.
4.15
. We shall call the Ehresmann connection on
\Xi
induced from one on
\mathscr{P}
along the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient map
\delta_{X}
the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient connection
.

The induced Ehresmann connections admit a standard (equivalent) definition in terms of smooth families of projectors, from which there emerges the definition of a coupling between the universal gauge field sourced by the connection 1-form on the principaloid bundle and (associated-)matter fields of interest.

Proposition 4.17
.

Adopt the notation of Prop.
4.15
and Thm.
3.29
. A (compatible) connection 1-form
\Theta\in\Omega^{1}(\mathscr{P},{\rm V}\mathscr{P})
on a principaloid
\mathscr{G}
-bundle
\mathscr{P}
induces a connection 1-form
\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}\in\Omega^{1}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX,{\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX))
on the
\mu_{X}
-extended bundle
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
with the defining properties

\displaystyle\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}\big|_{{\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\ }\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)}={\rm id}_{{\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\ }\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)}\qquad{\rm and}\qquad{\rm ker}\,\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}={\rm H}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\,.

Let
\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}\hskip-2.0pt:\pi_{\mathscr{P}}^{-1}(O_{i})\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }O_{i}\times\mathscr{G}
be local trivialisations of
\mathscr{P}
over an open cover
\{O_{i}\}_{i\in I}
of
\Sigma
, and let
\{A_{i}\}_{i\in I}
be the corresponding local data of
\Theta
. The induced connection 1-form is the
{\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)
-valued 1-form
\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}
with local presentations

\displaystyle\bigl(\widehat{\mathscr{P}\tau}{}_{i}^{-1\,*}\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}\bigr)(\sigma,g,x)={\rm id}_{{\rm T}\mathscr{G}}\big|_{g}+{\rm id}_{{\rm T}X}\big|_{x}-{\rm T}_{{\rm Id}_{t(g)}}r_{g}\circ A_{i}\bigl(\sigma,t(g)\bigr)\,,\qquad(\sigma,g,x)\in O_{i}\times\bigl(\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\,,\qquad i\in I\,,

written in terms of the local trivialisations

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathscr{P}\tau}{}_{i}\hskip-2.0pt:(\pi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1})^{-1}(O_{i})\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }O_{i}\times\bigl(\mathscr{G}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{s\,}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX\bigr)\,,\ \bigl(\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,g),x\bigr)\longmapsto(\sigma,g,x)

of
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
induced by the
\mathscr{P}\tau_{i}
.

The connection 1-form
\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}
is a compatible connection 1-form on the principaloid
\mathscr{G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X
-bundle
\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX
, in conformity with Prop.
4.7
.

Proof.

Obvious.
∎

Definition 4.18
.

Adopt the notation of Prop.

. Given a connection

on

and the corresponding connection
{\rm T}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)={\rm V}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)\oplus{\rm H}(\mathscr{P}\,\,\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{\mu_{X}}\hskip-2.0ptX)
on the

, the

-quotient connection 1-form
on the

-associated bundle

is a

with the property

In analogy with Prop.

, we readily establish

Proposition 4.19

and Prop.

. The

4.4.
Covariant derivatives of associated matter fields

The hitherto constructions provide us with a gauge-covariant differentiation of sections of the
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle, through which a coupling between the universal gauge field and the corresponding species of charged matter arises functionally.

Definition 4.21
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
4.18
. The
covariant derivative
of a section
\xi\in\Gamma(\Xi)
of the
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle
\Xi
of
\mathscr{P}

relative to
a
\mathscr{G}
-quotient connection 1-form
\Theta_{\Xi}
on
\Xi
is the
C^{\infty}(\Sigma,{\mathbb{R}})
-linear mapping

(4.48)

\displaystyle\nabla^{\Theta_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\xi\hskip-2.0pt:\Gamma({\rm T}\Sigma)\longrightarrow\Gamma(\xi^{*}{\rm V}\Xi),\mathcal{V}\longmapsto\Theta_{\Xi}\circ{\rm T}\xi(\mathcal{V})\equiv\nabla^{\Theta_{\Xi}}_{\mathcal{V}}\xi\,.

The verticalised differentiation thus defined exhibits the desired covariance properties.

Proposition 4.22
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
3.30
and
4.21
and Prop.
4.13
. Given an arbitrary gauge transformation
\Phi\in{\rm Gauge}(\mathscr{P})
of
\mathscr{P}
, let
\Theta_{\Xi}^{\Phi}
denote the
\mathscr{G}
-quotient connection on the
\lambda_{X}
-associated bundle
\Xi
induced from the gauge transform
\Theta^{\Phi}
of the connection 1-form
\Theta
. Furthermore, for an arbitrary section
\xi\in\Gamma(\Xi)
of
\Xi
, let
\xi^{\Phi}
denote the corresponding gauge transform of
\xi
:

\displaystyle\xi^{\Phi}\equiv\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\circ\xi\,.

The covariant derivative of
\xi
relative to
\Theta_{\Xi}
transforms
covariantly
as

\displaystyle\nabla^{\Theta^{\Phi}_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\bigl(\xi^{\Phi}\bigr)={\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\nabla^{\Theta_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\xi\,.

Proof.

Begin by noting that
\Theta_{\Xi}^{\Phi}
, being induced from
\Theta^{\Phi}
, can be understood as a shadow of the gauge transform
\widehat{\Theta}{}^{\Phi}_{X}
of
\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}
, the transform being given by the formula

\displaystyle\widehat{\Theta}{}^{\Phi}_{X}={\rm T}\bigl({\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}\circ{\rm T}\bigl({\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)\bigr)^{-1}\,,

see (
3.38
) and Prop.
4.13
. Accordingly, it satisfies—in the light of Eqs. (
4.47
) and (
4.35
)—the identity

(4.50)

\displaystyle\Theta_{\Xi}^{\Phi}\circ{\rm T}\delta_{X}={\rm T}\delta_{X}\circ\widehat{\Theta}{}^{\Phi}_{X}={\rm T}\bigl(\delta_{X}\circ{\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}\circ{\rm T}\bigl({\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)\bigr)^{-1}={\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\circ\delta_{X}\bigr)\circ\widehat{\Theta}{}_{X}\circ{\rm T}\bigl({\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)\bigr)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\Theta_{\Xi}\circ{\rm T}\bigl(\delta_{X}\circ{\rm Ext}_{X}(\Phi)^{-1}\bigr)={\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\Theta_{\Xi}\circ{\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)^{-1}\circ{\rm T}\delta_{X}\,,

from which the simple formula for the gauge-transform of
\Theta_{\Xi}
follows by the surjectivity of
{\rm T}\delta_{X}
:

\displaystyle\Theta_{\Xi}^{\Phi}={\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\Theta_{\Xi}\circ{\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)^{-1}\,.

Taking the latter into account, we verify the desired covariance in an explicit calculation:

\displaystyle\nabla^{\Theta^{\Phi}_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\bigl(\xi^{\Phi}\bigr)\equiv\Theta^{\Phi}_{\Xi}\circ{\rm T}\xi^{\Phi}={\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\Theta_{\Xi}\circ{\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)^{-1}\circ{\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\circ\xi\bigr)={\rm T}\bigl(\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)\circ\nabla^{\Theta_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\xi\,.

∎

At long last, we may write out the local presentation of the verticalised derivative, in which the gauge-matter field coupling becomes manifest.

Definition 4.23
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
4.21
and Prop.
4.8
. For every global section
\xi\in\Gamma(\Xi)
, with local data
\xi_{i}:={\rm pr}_{2}\circ\Xi\tau_{i}\circ\xi\big|_{O_{i}}\hskip-2.0pt:O_{i}\to X,\ i\in I
, we call the expression

\displaystyle\mathscr{D}^{{\rm A}_{i}}_{\cdot}\xi_{i}:={\rm pr}_{2}\circ{\rm T}(\Xi\tau_{i})\circ\nabla^{\Theta_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\xi\big|_{O_{i}}

the
local presentation of the covariant derivative
of
\xi

relative to

\Theta_{\Xi}
(in trivialisation
\Xi\tau_{i}
).

The presentation takes the form explicited in the following

Proposition 4.24
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
4.23
and Prop.
4.20
. The local presentation of the covariant derivative relative to
\Theta_{\Xi}
of a global section
\xi\in\Gamma(\Xi)
with local data
\xi_{i},\ i\in I
takes the form

(4.51)

\displaystyle\mathscr{D}^{A_{i}}_{\cdot}\xi_{i}(\sigma)={\rm T}_{\sigma}\xi_{i}-\alpha_{\mathscr{E}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X}\bigl(\xi_{i}(\sigma),{\rm Id}_{(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i})(\sigma)}\bigr)\circ A_{i}\bigl(\sigma,\bigl(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i}\bigr)(\sigma)\bigr)\,,\quad\sigma\in O_{i}\,.

Proof.

We calculate directly, with the help of Prop.
4.20
:

(4.53)

\displaystyle\mathscr{D}^{A_{i}}_{\cdot}\xi_{i}(\sigma)\equiv{\rm pr}_{2}\circ{\rm T}_{\xi(\sigma)}(\Xi\tau_{i})\circ\nabla^{\Theta_{\Xi}}_{\cdot}\xi(\sigma)\equiv{\rm pr}_{2}\circ{\rm T}_{\xi(\sigma)}(\Xi\tau_{i})\circ\Theta_{\Xi}\bigl(\xi(\sigma)\bigr)\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\xi

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\rm pr}_{2}\circ\bigl(\Xi\tau_{i}^{-1\,*}\Theta_{\Xi}\bigr)\bigl(\sigma,\xi_{i}(\sigma)\bigr)\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\bigl(\Xi\tau_{i}\circ\xi\bigr)

(4.55)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl({\rm id}_{{\rm T}_{\xi_{i}(\sigma)}X}-\alpha_{\mathscr{E}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X}\bigl(\xi_{i}(\sigma),{\rm Id}_{(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i})(\sigma)})\circ A_{i}\bigl(\sigma,\bigl(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i}\bigr)(\sigma)\bigr)\bigr)\bigl({\rm id}_{{\rm T}_{\sigma}\Sigma},{\rm T}_{\sigma}\xi_{i}\bigr)

(4.57)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\rm T}_{\sigma}\xi_{i}-\alpha_{\mathscr{E}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X}\bigl(\xi_{i}(\sigma),{\rm Id}_{(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i})(\sigma)}\bigr)\circ{\rm A}_{i}\bigl(\sigma,\bigl(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i}\bigr)(\sigma)\bigr)\,.

∎

4.5.
Applications of the associating construction

The findings presented in the previous (sub)sections provide us with a solid mathematical framework for addressing the issues raised in the opening paragraph, which we now discuss briefly in that framework.

The possibility of using associated principaloid bundles in the modelling of structure-group reduction suggests itself readily: Whenever, for a given Lie groupoid
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
and a subgroup
{\mathbb{B}}_{\rm red}(\mathscr{G})\subset{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
, identified as the reduced structure group in a field-theoretic setting of interest (
e.g.
, preserving an extra differential-geometric structure on
M
or
\mathscr{G}
), there exists a Lie groupoid
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 12.72224pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-12.72224pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}_{\rm red}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 26.94861pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 26.94861pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 26.94861pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M_{\rm red}}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
and a left
\mathscr{G}_{\rm red}
-module structure
(M,\mu_{M},\lambda_{M})
on
M
such that
\mathscr{G}_{\rm red}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{M}}M\cong\mathscr{G}
and
{\mathbb{B}}_{\rm red}(\mathscr{G})={\rm Im}\,\widetilde{\mu}{}^{*}_{M}
for the group homomorphism
\widetilde{\mu}{}^{*}_{M}:{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G}_{\rm red})\to{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
from Prop.
4.6
, then we may first erect a principaloid
\mathscr{G}_{\rm red}
-bundle
\mathscr{P}_{\rm red}\to\Sigma
with (unreduced) structure group
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G}_{\rm red})
, and subsequently associate with it a bundle
\mathscr{P}_{\rm red}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{M}}M\to\Sigma
by the action
\lambda_{M}
. In virtue of Prop.
4.7
, we thus obtain a principaloid
\mathscr{G}
-bundle with a structure group reduced to (an isomorphic image of)
{\mathbb{B}}_{\rm red}(\mathscr{G})
, as desired.

The other issue is of a more conceptual nature, as it concerns the modelling of multiple (different) charged-matter fields to which a single gauge field couples, the latter coming from a given principaloid bundle. Clearly, the induction mechanism for
\mathscr{G}
-quotient connections described in Prop.
4.15
paves the way to a systematic construction of invariants of the induced gauge groups
\Xi_{*}({\rm Gauge}(\mathscr{P}))
,
e.g.
, in terms of
B\lambda_{X}({\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G}))
-invariant tensors
8
8

8

Going beyond the minimal-coupling scheme is also possible, see: Sec.
10
.
on
X
. Indeed, a straightforward adaptation of the minimal-coupling scheme from Sec.
2
(see: the passage between (
2.11
) and (
2.12
)) associates to every such tensor field
\mathcal{T}\in\Gamma({\rm T}^{*}X^{\otimes n})^{B\lambda_{X}({\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G}))}
a smooth tensor field
\mathcal{T}[\Theta_{\Xi}]\in\Gamma(({\rm T}^{*}\pi_{\Xi}^{-1}\check{Y}_{\mathcal{O}})^{\otimes n})
on the total space of the surjective submersion
\check{\pi}_{\Xi}\hskip-2.0pt:\pi_{\Xi}^{-1}\check{Y}_{\mathcal{O}}\equiv\bigsqcup_{i\in I}\,\pi_{\Xi}^{-1}(O_{i})\to\Xi,\ (\Xi\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,x),i)\mapsto\Xi\tau_{i}^{-1}(\sigma,x)
with local restrictions

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}[\Theta_{\Xi}]\big|_{\pi_{\Xi}^{-1}(O_{i})}:=\Xi\tau_{i}^{*}\bigl(\mathcal{T}\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\circ\bigl(\Xi\tau_{i}^{-1\,*}\Theta_{\Xi}\bigr)^{\otimes n}\bigr)\equiv\mathcal{T}\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\circ\bigl({\rm T}\Xi\tau_{i}\circ\Theta_{\Xi}\bigr)^{\otimes n}\big|_{\pi_{\Xi}^{-1}(O_{i})}\in\Gamma\bigl({\rm T}^{*}\pi_{\Xi}^{-1}(O_{i})^{\otimes n}\bigr)

(see: Prop.
4.20
), obtained from
\mathcal{T}
through the minimal coupling of the local gauge field which is mediated by the verticalising
\mathscr{G}
-quotient connection 1-form from the covariant derivative (
4.48
) in a local presentation (
4.51
). The family manifestly descends—in the sheaf-theoretic sense—to a smooth tensor field

\displaystyle\underline{\mathcal{T}[\Theta_{\Xi}]}\in\Gamma\bigl({\rm T}^{*}\Xi^{\otimes n}\bigr)\,,\qquad\qquad\check{\pi}_{\Xi}^{*}\underline{\mathcal{T}[\Theta_{\Xi}]}=\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}[\Theta_{\Xi}]\,.

The latter is gauge invariant, as captured by the following identity, written for an arbitrary gauge transformation
\Phi\in{\rm Gauge}(\mathscr{P})
,

\displaystyle\Xi_{*}(\Phi)^{*}\underline{\mathcal{T}[\Theta_{\Xi}^{\Phi}]}=\underline{\mathcal{T}[\Theta_{\Xi}]}\,.

This implies the invariance of the pullback

\displaystyle\mathcal{T}[\xi,\Theta_{\Xi}]\equiv\xi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{T}[\Theta_{\Xi}]}

of the descended tensor along an arbitrary matter field
\xi\in\Gamma(\Xi)
,

\displaystyle\mathcal{T}[\xi^{\Phi},\Theta_{\Xi}^{\Phi}]=\mathcal{T}[\xi,\Theta_{\Xi}]\,,\quad\Phi\in{\rm Gauge}(\mathscr{P})\,.

Thus, the initial geometric problem is solved, but there arises a new
dynamical
one, which follows from the fact that the local gauge field
A_{i}
,
i.e.
, the local datum of the inducing connection 1-form
\Theta
, ‘lives’ not only on the spacetime
\Sigma\supset O_{i}
of the field theory, but also on the generically non-terminal manifold of units
M
of the structure groupoid of
\mathscr{P}
, and so requires a
choice
of a graph of a map
\varphi_{i}\hskip-2.0pt:O_{i}\to M
to couple to a charged-matter field as

(4.58)

\displaystyle A_{i}\bigl(\sigma,\varphi_{i}(\sigma)\bigr)\,,\quad\sigma\in O_{i}\,.

A natural model of such a graph is a local presentation
\mathscr{F}\tau_{i}\circ\varphi=({\rm id}_{O_{i}},\varphi_{i})
of a section
\varphi\in\Gamma(\mathscr{F})
of the distinguished shadow bundle. In view of its special rôle in the construction, we refer to
\mathscr{F}
and
\varphi
in what follows as the
Higgs bundle
and a
Higgs field
, respectively. If we are interested in the dynamics of
probe
matter fields, which do not affect a given gauge-field
background
, the above poses no additional technical difficulty, because we may simply fix the values of the gauge field on
all
allowed Higgs fields by declaring its
global
form
\Theta
once and for all. The problem arises whenever we choose to treat the gauge field
dynamically
,
i.e.
, when its preferred values are determined by a variational principle
jointly with
and
in relation to
those of the Higgs and (other) charged matter
sources
. We then encounter two natural scenarios in the setting under consideration:

•

The hybrid scenario
: The Higgs-restricted gauge field (
4.58
) is determined by a variational principle for a Yang–Mills–Higgs(-type) (YMH) theory, which couples the gauge field to the distinguished Higgs matter, and is then extended smoothly to an arbitrary background for charged-matter fields coming from the associated bundles
\Xi
. The most natural and elementary choice of the YMH dynamics is one in which the Higgs field
\varphi
becomes the dynamical source of the
curvature
of the gauge field, the latter being modelled in a standard manner—through local trivialisations (see:
[
KMS93
, Sec. 9.7]
)—on the
curvature of the connection

\Theta
,

\displaystyle R[\Theta]:=\Theta\circ[\cdot,\cdot]_{\Gamma({\rm T}\mathscr{P})}\circ\bigl(({\rm id}_{{\rm T}\mathscr{P}}-\Theta)\wedge({\rm id}_{{\rm T}\mathscr{P}}-\Theta)\bigr)\hskip-2.0pt:\bigwedge\hskip-3.0pt{}^{2}\hskip 1.0pt{\rm T}\mathscr{P}\longrightarrow{\rm V}\mathscr{P}\,.

The curvature measures an obstruction against integrability of the horizontal distribution
{\rm H}\mathscr{P}\equiv{\rm ker}\,\Theta
, see:
[
KMS93
, Sec. 9.4]
. It is not difficult to write down simple gauge invariants involving local presentations of
R[\Theta]
, further restricted to Higgs graphs in the YMH action functional, at least as long as there exists a metric
\kappa_{\mathscr{E}}\in\Gamma(S^{2}\mathscr{E}^{*})
on the tangent algebroid
\mathscr{E}
of
\mathscr{G}
invariant under the action of the group
\underline{{\rm T}C}({\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G}))
from Prop.
B.42
. Lie-algebroidal prototypes of such invariants were considered by Strobl and Kotov in
[
Str04
,
KS15
]
, and we shall provide their generalisations for arbitrary principaloid bundles in an upcoming work.

•

The multi-field scenario
: The gauge field is determined on the collection of images of
all
charged-matter fields in
\mathscr{F}
(obtained with the help of the respective bundle maps
\Upsilon_{X}
) by a variational principle for a (lagrangean) field theory in which every species of charged matter contributes
independently
to the curvature of the gauged field (
e.g.
, through a replica of the invariant from the previous point, but now restricted to local presentations of
\Upsilon_{X}\circ\xi
in sector
\Gamma(\Xi)\ni\xi
).

It is easy to see that both scenarios have serious shortcomings. In the former one, it is the fundamentally different ontological status of the matter fields—the Higgs field acts as a source for the gauge field, whereas the remaining matter fields are mere probes—that may seem unnatural, and even if it be viewed as a proposal for an
effective
field theory of a Higgs field ‘strongly’ coupled to the gauge field and remaining matter fields ‘weakly’ coupled to that field, it is still technically cumbersome as the background gauge field would have to be allowed to vary at intersections of the dynamical Higgs section with the
\Upsilon_{X}
-images of the other dynamical matter sections in
\mathscr{F}
, in a way dictated by the variational principle for the YMH sector. In the latter one, on the other hand, independent determination of the gauge field in each matter sector might lead to contradictions at the aforementioned intersections of critical matter sections, and it is far from obvious how to exclude such contradictions other than by manually overriding the principle of least action through imposition of a suitable ‘superselection rule’.

Luckily, there is a simple method to circumnavigate the above-mentioned problems in harmony with the distinguished status of the mother principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}
and its Higgs shadow
\mathscr{F}
. It consists in the imposition, on all classical configurations of charged-matter fields
\xi\in\Xi
, of the
Higgs alignment constraint

\displaystyle\Upsilon_{X\,*}(\xi)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{=}}\varphi\,,

the latter being written in terms of the map

\displaystyle\Upsilon_{X\,*}\hskip-2.0pt:\Gamma(\Xi)\longrightarrow\Gamma(\mathscr{F}),\ \xi\longmapsto\Upsilon_{X}\circ\xi\,,

and hence consistent with the gauge symmetry present,

\displaystyle\Upsilon_{X\,*}\bigl(\xi^{\Phi}\bigr)\equiv\bigl(\Upsilon_{X}\circ\Xi_{*}(\Phi)\bigr)(\xi)=\bigl(\mathscr{F}_{*}(\Phi)\circ\Upsilon_{X}\bigr)(\xi)\equiv\mathscr{F}_{*}(\Phi)\bigl(\Upsilon_{X\,*}(\xi)\bigr)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{=}}\mathscr{F}_{*}(\Phi)(\varphi)\equiv\varphi^{\Phi}\,,

see: (
4.37
). Indeed, it yields the identity (for
\xi_{i}
and
\varphi_{i}
as before)

(4.60)

\displaystyle\mathcal{T}[\xi,\Theta_{\Xi}](\sigma)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\mathcal{T}\circ\mathscr{D}^{A_{i}}_{\cdot}\xi_{i}(\sigma)^{\otimes n}=\mathcal{T}\circ\bigl({\rm T}_{\sigma}\xi_{i}-\alpha_{\mathscr{E}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X}\bigl(\xi_{i}(\sigma),{\rm Id}_{(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i})(\sigma)}\bigr)\circ A_{i}\bigl(\sigma,\bigl(\mu_{X}\circ\xi_{i}\bigr)(\sigma)\bigr)\bigr)^{\otimes n}

\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{=}}

\displaystyle\mathcal{T}\circ\bigl({\rm T}_{\sigma}\xi_{i}-\alpha_{\mathscr{E}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}X}\bigl(\xi_{i}(\sigma),{\rm Id}_{\varphi_{i}(\sigma)}\bigr)\circ A_{i}\bigl(\sigma,\varphi_{i}(\sigma)\bigr)\bigr)^{\otimes n}\,,

and so it ensures that the coupling between the matter field
\xi
and the gauge field is fully determined by the restriction of the latter to the underlying Higgs section. We shall study physical consequences of the Higgs alignment in a future work.

5.
The charged loop and its rigid symmetries

Below, we introduce a class of field theories whose inherently geometric functional definition, involving both: tensorial and cohomological objects on the configuration fibre, sets the stage for a nontrivial and structurally varied discussion of the gauge principle for groupoidal symmetries. The discussion features two conceptually related types of descent to the configuration bundle
\mathscr{F}
(in the spirit of Sec.
2
and Rem.
3.20
): the sheaf-theoretic descent of (minimally coupled) background tensors and the (2-)stacky descent of (connection-augmented) cohomological objects. Our choice of the field theories to be analysed can be defended independently on the grounds of their relevance in the context of—on one hand—the critical bosonic string theory on curved target spaces
[
Fri85
]
, and—on the other hand, and for a specific choice of the target space—the effective field theory of (slow) spinons in certain quantum spin chains
[
AH87
]
.

Definition 5.1
.

A
Polyakov–Alvarez–Gawȩdzki
(
PAG
)
\sigma
-model
is a triple

\displaystyle\bigl((\Sigma,\eta_{\Sigma}),(M,{\rm g}_{M},H_{M}),\mathcal{A}^{\sigma(M)}_{\rm DF}\bigr)\equiv\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}

which consists of

•

a compact oriented two-dimensional smooth metric
9
9

9

The signature of
\eta_{\Sigma}
does not play a rôle in the present considerations, and so shall be left unspecified.
manifold
(\Sigma,\eta_{\Sigma})
without boundary,
\partial\Sigma=\emptyset
, termed the
worldsheet
;

•

a smooth manifold
M
, termed the
target space
, endowed with a metric
{\rm g}_{M}\in\Gamma(S^{2}{\rm T}^{*}M)
and a closed differential 3-form
H_{M}\in Z^{3}_{\rm dR}(M)
with
2\pi
-integral periods,
{\rm Per}([H_{M}])\subset 2\pi{\mathbb{Z}}
;

•

a map

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}^{\sigma(M)}_{\rm DF}\hskip-2.0pt:C^{\infty}(\Sigma,M)\longrightarrow{\rm U}(1),\ \varphi\longmapsto\mathcal{A}^{\rm metr}_{\rm DF}[\varphi]\cdot\mathcal{A}^{\rm top}_{\rm DF}[\varphi]\equiv\mathcal{A}^{\sigma(M)}_{\rm DF}[\varphi]\,,

termed the
Dirac–Feynman
(
DF
)
amplitude
10
10

10

We stick to the formulation of the dynamics and the attendant nomenclature consistently used by Gawȩdzki
et al.
(see,
e.g.
,
[
RS09
,
GSW10
,
GSW13
]
) since the pioneering paper
[

, in which Dirac’s quantum-mechanical interpretation of the classical action functional
[

]
—subsequently employed by Feynman
[
Fey48
]
—was emphasised and put to work in a rigorous modelling of the dynamics and (Aharonov–Bohm-type) interference phases of extended distributions of topological charge in external gravitational and (higher) charge/gauge fields.
with components:

–

the (
Polyakov
)
metric amplitude

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}^{\rm metr}_{\rm DF}[\varphi]:={\rm exp}\left(-\tfrac{{\mathsf{i}}}{2}\,\int_{\Sigma}\,{\rm g}_{M}\bigl({\rm T}\varphi\,\overset{\wedge}{,}\star_{\eta_{\Sigma}}{\rm T}\varphi\bigr)\right)\,,

in which
{\rm T}\varphi
is regarded as a section of
{\rm T}^{*}\Sigma\otimes\varphi^{*}{\rm T}M
, and then the Hodge operator
\star_{\eta_{\Sigma}}
of
\eta_{\Sigma}
and the exterior product

affect the first tensor factors in
{\rm T}^{*}\Sigma
, whereas the target-space metric
{\rm g}_{M}
contracts the other tensor factors in
\varphi^{*}{\rm T}M
, so that the exponent acquires the interpretation of a metric norm of
{\rm T}\varphi
;

–

the (
Wess–Zumino
)

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}^{\rm top}_{\rm DF}[\varphi]:=\chi_{H_{M}}\bigl(\varphi(\Sigma)\bigr)\,,

determined by a degree-3 Cheeger–Simons differential character
\chi_{H_{M}}\in\widehat{H}{}^{3}(M,{\rm U}(1))
of curvature
H_{M}
(see: Def.
D.8
), or—equivalently (see: Thm.
D.9
)—by a gerbe
\mathcal{G}
of the same curvature, with
\chi_{H_{M}}\equiv{\rm Hol}_{\mathcal{G}}
(see: Def.
D.10
).

Remark 5.2
.

In local coordinates
\{\sigma^{a}\}^{a\in\{1,2\}}
near
\sigma\in\Sigma
and
\{\varphi^{\mu}\}^{\mu\in\overline{1,{\rm dim}M}}
near
\varphi(\sigma)\in M
, the integrand in the metric amplitude takes the familiar form

\displaystyle{\rm g}_{M}\bigl({\rm T}\varphi\,\overset{\wedge}{,}\star_{\eta_{\Sigma}}{\rm T}\varphi\bigr)=_{\rm loc}{\rm Vol}(\Sigma)\,\sqrt{|{\rm det}\,\eta_{\Sigma}|}\,\bigl(\eta_{\Sigma}^{-1}\bigr)^{ab}\,{\rm g}_{M\,\mu\nu}(\varphi)\,\partial_{a}\varphi^{\mu}\,\partial_{b}\varphi^{\nu}\,.

This, in conjunction with the co-defining property of the characters:

\displaystyle\forall\,c\in C_{3}(M)\hskip-2.0pt:\chi_{H_{M}}(\partial c)={\rm exp}\left({\mathsf{i}}\,\int_{c}\,H_{M}\right)\,,

leads to the interpretation of the above field theory as that of (metric-)minimal embeddings
\varphi\hskip-2.0pt:\Sigma\to M
perturbed by Lorentz-type forces

\displaystyle\imath_{\wedge^{2}{\rm T}\varphi({\rm Vol}(\Sigma)^{*})}H_{M}\,,

written in terms of (a representative of) the orientation
{\rm Vol}(\Sigma)^{*}\in\Gamma(\wedge^{2}{\rm T}\Sigma)\setminus\{{\boldsymbol{0}}\}
on
\Sigma
.

The point of departure of any application of the gauge principle is the identification of rigid symmetries of the field theory of interest. This we provide in

Definition 5.3
.

A (
large
)
rigid symmetry
of a PAG
\sigma
-model
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
from Def.
5.1
is a diffeomorphism
f\in{\rm Diff}(M)
with the following properties:

\displaystyle f^{*}{\rm g}_{M}={\rm g}_{M}\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad f\in{\rm Isom}(M,{\rm g}_{M})\,,

and

\displaystyle\forall\varphi\in C^{\infty}(M)\hskip-2.0pt:\mathcal{A}_{\rm DF}^{\rm top}[f\circ\varphi]=\mathcal{A}_{\rm DF}^{\rm top}[\varphi]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad f^{*}\mathcal{G}\cong\mathcal{G}\,.

A
tangential rigid symmetry
of
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
is a vector field
\mathcal{V}\in\Gamma({\rm T}M)
with the following properties:

\displaystyle\,{-\hskip-8.0pt\mathscr{L}}_{\mathcal{V}}{\rm g}_{M}=0\,,

and

\displaystyle\forall\,\varphi\in C^{\infty}(\Sigma,M)\hskip-2.0pt:\int_{\varphi(\Sigma)}\,\imath_{\mathcal{V}}H_{M}=0\,,

i.e.,

\displaystyle\exists\,\kappa_{\mathcal{V}}\in\Omega^{1}(M)\hskip-2.0pt:\imath_{\mathcal{V}}H_{M}=-{\mathsf{d}}\kappa_{\mathcal{V}}\,.

We shall call the assignment
\mathcal{V}\mapsto\kappa_{\mathcal{V}}
the
comomentum map
.

Remark 5.4
.

A derivation and an in-depth discussion of the above notion of symmetry, consistent with the definition of the PAG
\sigma
-model in terms of the differential character, can be found in
[
GSW10
, Sec. 2.2]
(see also:
[
RS09
]
). Note, in particular, that we demand the invariance under
f
(resp.
\mathcal{V}
) of each of the two terms in the DF amplitude independently. This is justified by the (physically motivated) requirement that the invariance hold true for an arbitrary metric
\eta_{\Sigma}
, the latter being regarded as an independent field in the theory under consideration (see, e.g.,
[
Pol81
]
). Alternative approaches to the concept of (tangential) symmetry of a
\sigma
-model with a gauge-fixed worldsheet metric have also been considered, see, e.g.,
[
CDJS17
]
. Note also, in this context, that there exist long-known dualities of charged-loop mechanics, such as T-duality
[
Bus88
,
Bus87
]
and the Hughes–Polchinsky duality
[
HP86
,
GIT90
]
(see also
[
Sus19
,
Sus20
,
Sus21
,
Sus23
]
for a recent application in the higher-(super)geometric setting), which mix the metric and topological degrees of freedom.

The above general discussion is placed in the groupoidal context of interest through the following

Definition 5.5
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
5.3
and
B.18
. Let
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
be a PAG
\sigma
-model. A Lie groupoid
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
shall be called a
rigid-symmetry model
for
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
if there exists a (nontrivial) subgroup
{\mathbb{B}}_{\sigma}(\mathscr{G})\subseteq{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
such that each diffeomorphism in
t_{*}({\mathbb{B}}_{\sigma}(\mathscr{G}))\subset{\rm Diff}(M)
is a rigid symmetry of
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
. The subgroup
{\mathbb{B}}_{\sigma}(\mathscr{G})
shall be referred to as a
rigid groupoidal symmetry group of

\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
.

Example 5.6
.

Consider a compact simple and simply connected Lie group
{\rm G}
with tangent Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}\equiv{\rm Lie}({\rm G})
. On the group manifold, we find a family of Cartan–Killing metrics

\displaystyle{\rm g}_{\rm CK}=-\tfrac{{\mathsf{k}}}{4\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}\otimes\theta_{\rm L}\bigr)\,,\quad{\mathsf{k}}\in{\mathbb{R}}\,,

and a family of Cartan 3-forms

\displaystyle H_{\rm C}=\tfrac{{\mathsf{k}}}{12\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}\wedge[\cdot,\cdot]\circ\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}\wedge\theta_{\rm L}\bigr)\bigr)\,,

both written in terms of the left-invariant Maurer–Cartan form
\theta_{\rm L}=\delta_{\rm L}\log({\rm id}_{\rm G})\in\Omega^{1}({\rm G})\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathfrak{g}
(the left logarithmic derivative of
{\rm id}_{\rm G}
, see:
[
HN12
]
), with the understanding that the (antisymmetrised) tensoring takes place in the differential-form factor. Here, the trace
{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}
over
\mathfrak{g}
is normalised so that

\displaystyle{\rm Per}(H_{\rm C})\subset 2\pi{\mathbb{Z}}\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad{\mathsf{k}}\in{\mathbb{Z}}\,,

see, e.g.,
[
Gaw00
]
. We further constrain the
level

{\mathsf{k}}
as
{\mathsf{k}}\in{\mathbb{N}}
in order to obtain the standard sign in front of the metric factor after the Wick rotation. The 3-form
H_{\rm C}
now geometrises as the
{\mathsf{k}}{}^{\rm th}
tensor power
\mathcal{G}_{\rm b}^{\otimes{\mathsf{k}}}\equiv\mathcal{G}_{\mathsf{k}}
of Meinrenkren’s basic gerbe
\mathcal{G}_{\rm b}
over
{\rm G}

[
Mei03
]
(see: Defs.
D.4
and
D.10
). The ensuing PAG
\sigma
-model is termed the Wess–Zumino–Novikov–Witten (WZNW) model
[
Wit84
]
.

The group
{\rm G}
is the object manifold of the action groupoid
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G}\equiv\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 14.73613pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-14.73613pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{{\rm G}\times{\rm G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 28.9625pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 28.9625pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 28.9625pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\rm G}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
with
(s,t,{\rm Id},{\rm Inv})=({\rm pr}_{2},{\rm Ad},(e,\cdot),({\rm Inv}_{\rm G}\circ{\rm pr}_{1},{\rm Ad}))
, which furnishes a rigid-symmetry model for this field theory, of particular relevance to the study of its (maximally symmetric) defects
[
FSW08
,
RS11
,
Sus22
]
. The large symmetry induces a
\mathfrak{g}
-indexed family of tangential symmetries:

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}^{\rm G}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm G}\times\mathfrak{g}\longrightarrow{\rm T}{\rm G},\ (g,X)\longmapsto(L_{X}-R_{X})(g)\equiv\mathcal{K}^{\rm G}_{X}(g)\,,

i.e., the fundamental vector field for the action
{\rm Ad}
, with the left-invariant
L_{X}\in\Gamma({\rm T}{\rm G})
and the right-invariant
R_{X}\in\Gamma({\rm T}{\rm G})
vector fields on
{\rm G}
,

\displaystyle L_{X}(g)=\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}t}\big|_{t=0}\bigl(g\cdot{\rm exp}(tX)\bigr)\,,\qquad\qquad R_{X}(g)=\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}t}\big|_{t=0}\bigl({\rm exp}(tX)\cdot g\bigr)\,.

The corresponding comomentum map reads

\displaystyle\kappa_{\rm C}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm G}\times\mathfrak{g}\longrightarrow{\rm T}^{*}{\rm G},\ (g,X)\longmapsto-\tfrac{\textrm{${\mathsf{k}}$}}{4\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\textrm{$\mathfrak{g}$}}\bigl(X\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}(g)+\theta_{\rm R}(g)\bigr)\bigr)\equiv-\tfrac{{\mathsf{k}}}{4\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl(X\,t_{a}\bigr)\,\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}^{a}(g)+\theta_{\rm R}^{a}(g)\bigr)\,.

Above,
\{t_{a}\}_{a\in\overline{1,{\rm dim}\,{\rm G}}}
is an arbitrary basis of
\mathfrak{g}
, and
\theta_{\rm H}=\theta_{\rm H}^{a}\otimes t_{a},\ H\in\{{\rm L},{\rm R}\}
, with
\theta_{\rm R}=\delta_{\rm R}\log({\rm id}_{\rm G})
the right-invariant Maurer–Cartan form on
{\rm G}
. Note the properties:

\displaystyle\imath_{\mathcal{K}^{\rm G}_{X}}\kappa_{\rm C}(Y)=-\imath_{\mathcal{K}^{\rm G}_{Y}}\kappa_{\rm C}(X)\,,\qquad\qquad\kappa_{\rm C}\bigl({\rm T}_{e}{\rm Ad}_{h}(X)\bigr)={\rm Ad}_{h^{-1}}^{*}\bigl(\kappa_{\rm C}(X)\bigr)\,,

written for arbitrary
X,Y\in\mathfrak{g}
and
h\in{\rm G}
.

6.
The classic pathway to groupoidal configurational descent

We now proceed to briefly review the gauge principle for group-modelled symmetries in the setting of the PAG
\sigma
-model
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
from Def.
5.1
, as worked out by Gawȩdzki, Waldorf and the Author in
[
GSW10
,
GSW13
]
. Our goal is to identify its key structural elements and to put them in a form and context which render the whole construction amenable to subsequent natural generalisation. In so doing, we turn, once more, to the narrative, descriptive mode of exposition, referring the Reader to the original works for the relevant propositions and proofs.

The point of departure of our considerations is a choice of subgroup
{\rm G}\subset{\rm Isom}(M,{\rm g}_{M})
of isometries of a given
\sigma
-model target
M
, with smooth action
\lambda\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm G}\times M\to M
, and with the additional property

(6.1)

\displaystyle\forall\ X\in\mathfrak{g}\ \exists\ \kappa_{X}\in\Omega^{1}(M)\hskip-2.0pt:\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{X}}H_{M}=-{\mathsf{d}}\kappa_{X}\,,

stated for the tangent Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}\equiv{\rm Lie}({\rm G})
of
{\rm G}
, in terms of the fundamental vector field
11
11

11

The sign ‘-’ in the definition ensures that
\mathcal{K}
is a Lie-algebra homomorphism rather than an
anti
-homomorphism.
of
\lambda
,

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}\hskip-2.0pt:M\times\mathfrak{g}\longrightarrow{\rm T}M,\ (m,X)\longmapsto{\rm T}_{(e,m)}\lambda\bigl(-X,{\boldsymbol{0}}_{{\rm T}M}(m)\bigr)\equiv\mathcal{K}_{X}(m)\,.

Note that we may view the ensuing comomentum map as a vertical vector-bundle morphism
