with the domain canonically identified with the total space of the tangent algebroid
\mathfrak{g}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
of the underlying action groupoid
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
, see: Ex.
B.37
.

In view of the following identity (see:
[
GSW13
, Prop. 2.11]
), valid for all forms
\eta,\zeta\in\Omega^{\bullet}(M)
, all
(g,m)\in{\rm G}\times M
, and in a basis
\{t_{a}\}_{a\in\overline{1,{\rm dim}\,{\rm G}}}
of
\mathfrak{g}
, and written in the shorthand notation
\mathcal{K}_{t_{a}}\equiv\mathcal{K}_{a}
,

\displaystyle\lambda^{*}\eta(g,m)=\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\,\tfrac{(-1)^{n}}{n!}\,\widetilde{\imath}{}_{\mathcal{K}\circ\theta_{\rm L}(g)}^{n}\lambda_{g}^{*}\eta\right)(m)\,,\qquad\qquad\widetilde{\imath}{}_{\mathcal{K}\circ\theta_{\rm L}(g)}\zeta(m):=\theta^{a}_{\rm L}(g)\wedge\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{a}}\zeta(m)\,,

the existence of the comomentum implies the relation

(6.2)

\displaystyle\Delta^{(3)}_{(0)}H_{M}={\mathsf{d}}\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]\,,

expressed in terms of the
0^{\rm th}
Dupont operator
\Delta^{(\bullet)}_{(0)}=\lambda^{*}-{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}
of the simplicial nerve
N_{\bullet}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M)
of the action groupoid, see: Def.
C.3
and Ex.
C.4
, and of a distinguished 2-form on the latter’s arrow manifold:

(6.3)

\displaystyle\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\kappa_{a}\wedge{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\theta_{\rm L}^{a}-\tfrac{1}{2}\,{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{a}}\kappa_{b}\bigr)\,{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}^{a}\wedge\theta_{\rm L}^{b}\bigr)\in\Omega^{2}({\rm G}\times M)\,,

with
\kappa_{t_{a}}\equiv\kappa_{a}
. Invoking Thm.
D.3
, we infer that there is a flat gerbe
\mathcal{D}_{0}\in\mathcal{W}^{3}({\rm G}\times M;0)
and a 1-isomorphism

\displaystyle\Upsilon\hskip-2.0pt:\lambda^{*}\mathcal{G}\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]}\otimes\mathcal{D}_{0}\,.

These observations prepare the ground for the formulation of the gauging procedure, whose objective is to induce a
\sigma
-model background—
i.e.
, a metric tensor and a gerbe—on the total space of the associated bundle
P\times_{\lambda}M
from the original one
({\rm g}_{M},\mathcal{G})
on
M
.

First, we consider the topological component of the background—the gerbe
\mathcal{G}
. We begin by pulling it back to the total space of the extended bundle
P\times M
along the moment map
{\rm pr}_{2}\hskip-2.0pt:P\times M\to M
of the principal
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-bundle from Ex.
4.9
, and subsequently ask about the necessary conditions for the descent of the pullback to the bundle’s base
P\times_{\lambda}M
. By the previously reviewed construction, the surjective submersion
\pi_{\sim}\hskip-2.0pt:P\times M\to P\times_{\lambda}M
is, in fact, a principal
{\rm G}
-bundle, and so the conditions of descent are determined by the following specialisation of a more general result, due essentially to Stevenson
[
Ste00
]
, which we review and employ in Sec.
8
.

Theorem 6.1
.

[
GSW10
, Thm. 5.3]

Let
{\rm G}
be a Lie group, and let
X
be a
{\rm G}
-manifold with smooth action
\lambda_{X}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm G}\times X\to X
. Whenever the orbispace
X//{\rm G}
carries a smooth structure, and
X
fibres principally over it (e.g., when
\lambda_{X}
is free and proper), there exists a canonical equivalence

\displaystyle\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X//{\rm G})\cong\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X)^{{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda_{X}}\hskip-1.0ptX}

between the bicategory of gerbes over
X//{\rm G}
and that of
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}X
-equivariant gerbes over
X
, see: Def.
D.14
.

As a corollary to the last result, we infer that the isoclass of the gerbe
\mathcal{I}_{\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]}\otimes\mathcal{D}_{0}
encountered earlier constitutes an obstruction to a
direct
descent of
{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathcal{G}
to the associated bundle
P\times_{\lambda}M
. As demonstrated in
[
GSW10
]
, the component of this anomaly sourced by a non-vanishing comomentum,
\mathcal{I}_{\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]}
, can be neutralised though a procedure which employs the connection 1-form
\mathcal{A}
on the first cartesian factor of the base
P\times M
of the pullback gerbe
{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathcal{G}
. Indeed, assuming
\mathcal{G}
trivial,
\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{I}_{B}
, and endowed with a
{\rm G}
-invariant curving
B\in\Omega^{2}(M)^{\rm G}
, and further restricting to the topologically trivial case
P\cong\Sigma\times{\rm G}
with a global gauge field
A=A^{a}\otimes t_{a}\in\Omega^{1}(\Sigma)\otimes\mathfrak{g}
for the sake of simplicity, we find ourselves in the régime of applicability of the minimal-coupling scheme of Eq. (
2.11
). The latter takes the form

\displaystyle{\rm Hol}_{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}[A]}\bigl(({\rm id}_{\Sigma},\varphi)(\Sigma)\bigr)\,,\qquad\varphi\in C^{\infty}(\Sigma,M)

for an
A
-augmented gerbe

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}[A]={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{\kappa[A]}\,,

expressed in terms of the 2-form

(6.4)

\displaystyle\kappa[A]={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\kappa_{a}\wedge{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}A^{a}-\tfrac{1}{2}\,{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{a}}\kappa_{b}\bigr)\,{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\bigl(A^{a}\wedge A^{b}\bigr)\in\Omega^{2}(\Sigma\times M)\,,

to be compared with (
6.3
). For the holonomy of the
A
-augmented gerbe to be gauge-invariant, we need to ensure that the comomentum satisfy additional conditions, to wit, that it

(CG1)

be
{\rm G}
-equivariant

\displaystyle\kappa\circ\bigl(\lambda_{g}\times{\rm T}_{e}{\rm Ad}_{g}\bigr)=\lambda_{g^{-1}}^{*}\circ\kappa\,,\quad g\in{\rm G}\,;

(CG2)

define an isotropic distribution

\displaystyle\mathscr{C}_{\sigma}\equiv(\mathcal{K},\kappa)(M\times\mathfrak{g})\subset{\rm T}M\oplus{\rm T}^{*}M\equiv{\rm E}^{1,1}M

relative to the non-degenerate pairing

\displaystyle\left\langle\cdot,\cdot\right\rangle\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm E}^{1,1}M\times{\rm E}^{1,1}M\longrightarrow{\mathbb{R}},\ \bigl((v_{1},\omega_{1}),(v_{2},\omega_{2})\bigr)\longmapsto\tfrac{1}{2}\,\bigl(\omega_{2}(v_{1})+\omega_{1}(v_{2})\bigr)\,.

It is worth noting that Hitchin’s generalised tangent bundle
{\rm E}^{1,1}M
, thus arising naturally in the present setting, carries a richer structure
[
Hit03
]
, which helps to clarify the geometric meaning of the above conditions. Namely, it carries a Courant bracket

(6.7)

\displaystyle\lsem\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rsem_{\rm C}^{H_{M}}

\displaystyle\hskip-2.0pt:

\displaystyle\Gamma({\rm E}^{1,1}M)\times\Gamma({\rm E}^{1,1}M)\longrightarrow\Gamma({\rm E}^{1,1}M)

\displaystyle\bigl((\mathcal{V}_{1},\omega_{1}),(\mathcal{V}_{2},\omega_{2})\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl([\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}]_{TM},\,{-\hskip-8.0pt\mathscr{L}}_{\mathcal{V}_{1}}\omega_{2}-\,{-\hskip-8.0pt\mathscr{L}}_{\mathcal{V}_{2}}\omega_{1}-\tfrac{1}{2}\,{\mathsf{d}}\bigl(\imath_{\mathcal{V}_{1}}\omega_{2}-\imath_{\mathcal{V}_{2}}\omega_{1}\bigr)+\imath_{\mathcal{V}_{1}}\imath_{\mathcal{V}_{2}}H_{M}\bigr)

twisted by
H_{M}
à la Ševera–Weinstein
[
ŠW01
]
, which endowes
{\rm E}^{1,1}M
with the structure of a Courant algebroid
({\rm E}^{1,1}M,\lsem\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rsem_{\rm C}^{H_{M}},\left\langle\cdot,\cdot\right\rangle,{\rm pr}_{1})
(see:
[
Dor87
,
CW88
]
). The bracket is readily shown to close on the symmetry distribution
\mathscr{C}_{\sigma}
. The conditions for the gaugeability of the rigid symmetry
{\rm G}
in the simplified scenario considered above now translate—upon linearisation of the group action—into a statement of homomorphicity of the map

\displaystyle(\mathcal{K},\kappa)\hskip-2.0pt:\bigl(M\times\mathfrak{g},\mathcal{K},[\cdot,\cdot]_{\mathfrak{g}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M}\bigr)\longrightarrow\bigl({\rm E}^{1,1}M,{\rm pr}_{1},\lsem\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rsem_{\rm C}^{H_{M}}\bigr)\,,

This fact was first observed in the context of gauging in
[
Sus12
]
(see also:
[
GSW13
]
), with a field-theoretic inspiration coming from
[
AS05
]
. It reflects the deeper structural relation between Hitchin’s generalised geometry and the higher geometry of gerbes
[
Hit03
,
Gua03
,
Sus12
]
.

The above observation, derived for trivial gerbes with a
{\rm G}
-invariant curving, may now—and was—turned into a postulate for gerbes of
arbitrary
topology: Any such gerbe
\mathcal{G}
is to be pulled back to
P\times M
along the moment map
{\rm pr}_{2}
and subsequently augmented by a trivial gerbe with curving determined by a comomentum
\kappa
, satisfying the conditions listed above, and with the obvious replacement of the trivial gauge field by the connection 1-form
\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}^{a}\otimes t_{a}\in\Omega^{1}(P)\otimes\mathfrak{g}
. Thus, we obtain an
\mathcal{A}
-augmented gerbe

(6.8)

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}[\mathcal{A}]={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{\kappa[\mathcal{A}]}

over the extended bundle
P\times M
, with

(6.9)

\displaystyle\kappa[\mathcal{A}]={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\kappa_{a}\wedge{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\mathcal{A}^{a}-\tfrac{1}{2}\,{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{a}}\kappa_{b}\bigr)\,{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\bigl(\mathcal{A}^{a}\wedge\mathcal{A}^{b}\bigr)\in\Omega^{2}(P\times M)\,.

Its properties relevant to the gauging procedure under consideration are summarised in

Theorem 6.2
.

[
GSW10
, Prop. 5.5]

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.14
. Let
{\rm G}
be a Lie group with tangent Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}
, and let
(M,\lambda)
be a
{\rm G}
-manifold with a gerbe
\mathcal{G}\in\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(M)
over it, and with a comomentum
\kappa
determined by the curvature
H_{M}
of
\mathcal{G}
as in (
6.1
), and satisfying conditions
(CG1)
and
(CG2)
. Moreover, let
P
be a principal
{\rm G}
-bundle over a compact closed orientable two-dimensional base
\Sigma
, equipped with a connection 1-form
\mathcal{A}\in\Omega^{1}(P)\otimes\mathfrak{g}
. If the gerbe admits a
\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]
-twisted
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-equivariant structure
(\Upsilon,\gamma)
, with the 2-form
\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]
from Eq. (
6.3
), then the corresponding
\mathcal{A}
-augmented gerbe
\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}[\mathcal{A}]
from Eq. (
6.8
) carries a canonical
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-equivariant structure, and so it canonically induces a gerbe
\underline{\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{A}]}\in\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(P\times_{\lambda}M)
over the associated bundle
P\times_{\lambda}M
, unique up to 1-isomorphism, whose pullback along
\pi_{\sim}
is (
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-equivariantly) 1-isomorphic to
\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}[\mathcal{A}]
. Furthermore, the holonomy of
\underline{\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{A}]}
is invariant under gauge transformations in the sense captured by the identity (see: Eq. (
2.9
))

\displaystyle\forall\ (\varphi,\chi)\in\Gamma(P\times_{\lambda}M)\times\Gamma({\rm Ad}\,P)\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm Hol}_{\underline{\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{A}^{\chi}]}}\bigl((\chi\circ\varphi)(\Sigma)\bigr)={\rm Hol}_{\underline{\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{A}]}}\bigl(\varphi(\Sigma)\bigr)\,.

Two comments are in order at this point, which shall play an important rôle when we come to discuss a generalisation of the present scenario: First of all, the existence of a
\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]
-twisted
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-equivariant structure on
\mathcal{G}
necessitates that the identity

(6.10)

\displaystyle\Delta^{(2)}_{(1)}\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]=0\,,

expressed in terms of the
1^{\rm st}
Dupont operator
\Delta^{(\bullet)}_{(1)}
of
N_{\bullet}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M)
, hold true. Secondly, the induction of an
un
twisted
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-equivariant structure on
\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}[\mathcal{A}]
hinges on the identity

\displaystyle\widetilde{\lambda}{}^{*}\bigl(\kappa[\mathcal{A}]\bigr)+\bigl({\rm Inv}\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)^{*}\bigl(\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]\bigr)={\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\bigl(\kappa[\mathcal{A}]\bigr)

over the domain
(P\times M)\times_{M}({\rm G}\times M)
of the
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
-action (
2.3
). The identity uses
both
properties of the comomentum, (CG1) and (CG2), assumed in the definition of the
\mathcal{A}
-augmented gerbe. Finally, note that the existence of a coherent pair
(\Upsilon,\gamma)
is, in general, obstructed topologically (in particular, it calls for the vanishing of
[\mathcal{D}_{0}]
), and the obstruction, as well as a classification of inequivalent such pairs whenever the obstruction vanishes, is amenable to a cohomological analysis in the natural setting of
{\rm G}
-equivariant cohomology
[
Tu20
]
, see:
[
GSW10
]
. We provide its suitable generalisation to the groupoidal case and a detailed exposition in Sec.
9
.

We finish the construction of the gauged
\sigma
-model by defining its metric term. The point of departure is, in this case, the symmetric tensor
\underline{{\rm g}_{M}[\mathcal{A}]}
on
P\times_{\lambda}M
descended from the family of
\Sigma
-local minimally coupled ones
\{\widetilde{\rm g}{}_{M}[A_{i}]\}_{i\in I}
as described in the passage between (
2.11
) and (
2.12
). We evaluate it on the tangent morphism
{\rm T}\varphi
for
\varphi\in\Gamma(P\times_{\lambda}M)
, viewed as a section of
{\rm T}^{*}\Sigma\otimes\varphi^{*}{\rm T}(P\times_{\lambda}M)
and, as such, suitably acted upon in the domain (as before), whereby we obtain the metric coupling

\displaystyle\left\langle\underline{{\rm g}_{M}[\mathcal{A}]},{\rm T}\varphi^{\otimes 2}\right\rangle=\underline{{\rm g}_{M}[\mathcal{A}]}\bigl({\rm T}\varphi\,\overset{\wedge}{,}\star_{\eta_{\Sigma}}{\rm T}\varphi\bigr)\,.

Altogether, then, in the notation used hitherto, we arrive at the definition of the PAG
\sigma
-model with the symmetry
\lambda
gauged:

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}^{\sigma(P\times_{\lambda}M)}_{\rm DF}\hskip-2.0pt:\Gamma(P\times_{\lambda}M)\longrightarrow{\rm U}(1),\ \varphi\longmapsto{\rm exp}\left(-\tfrac{{\mathsf{i}}}{2}\,\int_{\Sigma}\,\underline{{\rm g}_{M}[\mathcal{A}]}\bigl({\rm T}\varphi\,\overset{\wedge}{,}\star_{\eta_{\Sigma}}{\rm T}\varphi\bigr)\right)\cdot{\rm Hol}_{\underline{\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{A}]}}\bigl(\varphi(\Sigma)\bigr)\,.

We shall next generalise the above reasoning to the case of a symmetry modelled on an arbitrary Lie groupoid, and of the shadow of the corresponding principaloid bundle.

Remark 6.3
.

It deserves to be noted that the idea of configurational reduction
M\searrow M//{\rm G}
, discussed abstractly at the end of Sec.
2
, admits an interesting concretisation in the setting of the gauged PAG
\sigma
-model whenever the gauge field trivialises (i.e., e.g., locally) and
M
fibres principally over the smooth quotient
M/{\rm G}
in such a way that
{\rm g}_{M}
induces a non-degenerate metric on the fibres. As demonstrated directly in
[
GSW13
]
, the variable—in conformity with the discussion in Sec.
2
—background gauge field may then be integrated out, producing an emergent
\sigma
-model background: a
{\rm G}
-basic metric

\displaystyle\widetilde{\rm g}{}_{M}={\rm g}_{M}+X^{ab}\,\bigl(\kappa_{a}\otimes\kappa_{b}-\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{a}\otimes\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{b}\bigr)+Y^{ab}\,\bigl(\kappa_{a}\otimes\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{b}+\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{a}\otimes\kappa_{b}\bigr)\,,

and an untwisted
{\rm G}
-equivariant gerbe

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}=\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{B}\,,\qquad\qquad B=\tfrac{1}{2}\,Y^{ab}\,\bigl(\kappa_{a}\wedge\kappa_{b}-\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{a}\otimes\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{b}\bigr)+X^{ab}\,\kappa_{a}\wedge\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{b}\,,

both written in terms of the
{\rm g}_{M}
-contracted fundamental vector field
\mathcal{K}^{\flat}_{a}={\rm g}_{M}(\mathcal{K}^{M}_{a},\cdot)
, and of the matrices
(X^{ab})\equiv X=E^{-1}
and
(Y^{ab})\equiv Y=h^{-1}\,c\,E^{-1}
determined by the background matrix
E=h-c\,h^{-1}\,c
, with
h=({\rm g}_{M}(\mathcal{K}^{M}_{a},\mathcal{K}^{M}_{b}))
and
c=(\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{a}}\kappa_{b})
. Thus, in the special situation just described, the
\sigma
-model descends to
M/{\rm G}
along
\pi\hskip-2.0pt:M\to M/{\rm G}
, with the induced background
(\underline{{\rm g}},\underline{\mathcal{G}})
such that
\pi^{*}\underline{{\rm g}}=\widetilde{\rm g}{}_{M}
and
\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}\cong\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}
.

7.
Reduction: Holonomicity and isometricity

In this section, we take the first step towards a generalisation of the gauge principle of Sec.
6
to arbitrary structure Lie groupoids
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
, and so also to arbitrary principal
\mathscr{G}
-bundles
(\mathscr{P},\mathscr{F})
in a given slice
{\rm{\bf Bun}}(\Sigma)/\Sigma
. In this first step, we consider the relevant tensorial background on the simplicial nerve
N_{\bullet}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)
of
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
, and the way in which it constrains our choice of the structure group. The latter now becomes functionally separated from the structure groupoid in a pronounced manner. We shall lift our findings to the higher geometry behind the tensors in Sec.
8
.

The highly structured nature of the prototype reviewed in the previous section suggests an immitation, which, however, becomes obscured by the various non-generic simplifications present in the prototypical construction:

•

an
a-priori
choice of the symmetry model
{\rm G}
, tailored to the extra geometric structure on
M
(the metric
{\rm g}_{M}
and the 3-form field
H_{M}
) and hence controlling the reduction of the structure group to the subgroup
\iota({\rm G})
from Ex.
B.11
, the latter coinciding with the
de-facto
structure groupoid
\mathbf{B}{\rm G}
;

•

the product form of the arrow manifold
{\rm G}\times M
, and the resultant simple factorisation of the twist
\kappa[\theta_{\rm L}]
, with the
M
-factor coming directly from the tangential-symmetry analysis of the DF amplitude prior to the gauging;

•

the global triviality of the underlying Lie algebroid
\mathfrak{g}\times M\to M
, and the resulting non-generic structure of the standard connection 1-form on the principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}=P\times M
, determined by a symmetry Lie algebra-valued 1-form
\mathcal{A}\in\Omega^{1}(P)\otimes\mathfrak{g}
, to which the comomentum may couple directly in the augmentation procedure (
6.8
);

In the light of the discussion of Sec.
4
, we could follow the pattern delineated in the previous section directly by starting with a given (higher-)geometric structure on a manifold
M
and fixing an
external
Lie groupoid that stabilises that structure (or integrates its tangential rigid symmetries). The groupoid would then become the basic ingredient of the associating construction. This is, most certainly, a legitimate bottom-up approach to the question of the gauging of categorified rigid symmetries. In what follows, though, we take a reverse approach, in which the structure groupoid
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
is given
a priori
(
e.g.
, as a symmetry of some initial structure on the manifold
M
), and a reduction of the attendant group
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
is enforced by the subsequent adjunction of extra geometric structure on its object manifold. As it happens, this scheme, emphasising the reduction mechanism (akin to classic ones, such as,
e.g.
, an isometric structure-group reduction on a vector bundle that accompanies the introduction of a metric), enables us to make contact with long-known and important constructions, such as that of a symplectic groupoid, which subsequently leads to the emergence of lagrangean bisections, see:
[
Wei87
,
CDW87
,
Ryb01
]
.

In this top-down approach, and upon relinquishing the non-genericity of the motivating construction, we need to carefully define the point of departure in our considerations. While it is completely straightforward in the case of tensorial components of the extra geometric structure on
M
, for which the right notion is that of
invariance
under the shadow action
t_{*}
of the (reduced) structure group within
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
, dealing with charge fields, such as the 3-form field
H_{M}
, and the associated higher-geometric constructs, such as the gerbe
\mathcal{G}
, calls for a more refined organising principle. This we read off from the discussion at the end of Sec.
2
, taken in conjunction with the main result of the seminal work
[
BSS76
]
of Bott, Schulman and Stasheff (see also:
[
Dup76
,
Dup88
]
), which is the extended de Rham Theorem in the relevant adaptation (see: Eq. (
2.14
) and Def.
C.8
)

\displaystyle H^{\bullet}({\rm B}\mathscr{G})=H^{\bullet}_{\rm BSS}\bigl(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt\bigr)\,.

Thus, viewing the gauging implemented by principaloid bundles as a field-theoretic mechanism of configurational descent, we are led to assume the existence of a
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant extension
of the tensorial background
H_{M}
as the basis of our considerations in the present section. That extension shall subsequently be geometrised coherently in Sec.
8
.

An extension postulated above takes the general form

\displaystyle(H_{M},\rho,\alpha,\beta)\in\Omega^{3}(M)\oplus\Omega^{2}(\mathscr{G})\oplus\Omega^{1}(\mathscr{G}_{2})\oplus\Omega^{0}(\mathscr{G}_{3})\,,

with

\displaystyle D_{(3)}(H_{M},\rho,\alpha,\beta)=0

for the BSS coboundary operator
D_{(3)}
from Def.
C.8
. The first of the three identities mixing components of the extension of different form-degrees reads

(7.1)

\displaystyle{\rm d}\rho=\Delta^{(3)}_{(0)}H_{M}\,,

and so it reproduces the familiar identity (
6.2
) upon specialisation. In conjunction with the anticipated geometrisation

(7.2)

\displaystyle\Upsilon\hskip-2.0pt:t^{*}\mathcal{G}\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }s^{*}\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{\rho}\,,

it acquires a meaningful physical interpretation of the (hyper)cohomological datum of a
\mathcal{G}
-bi-brane, which yields—through a variant of Gawȩdzki’s transgression map from
[
Gaw88
]
discussed at length in
[
Sus11a
]
—a prequantisation of the classical rigid symmetry modelled by
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
, see:
[
FSW08
,
RS09
]
and
[
Sus11a
,
Sus22
]
. It is then natural to enquire about conditions under which the corresponding worldsheet defect admits self-intersections, which are bound to arise in the quantised field theory
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
,
e.g.
, through factorisation of path integrals, see:
[
RS09
]
. The detailed analysis of
[
RS09
]
yields the necessary condition, to be satisfied by the extending 2-form
\rho
—it reads:

(7.3)

\displaystyle\Delta^{(2)}_{(1)}\rho=0\,,

and so it yields the formerly encountered identity (
6.10
) upon specialisation. Altogether, then, we are led—by our physical argument—to assume the very peculiar form of the extension (see: Def.
C.8
):

\displaystyle(H_{M},\rho,0,0)\in{\rm Tot}^{3}\bigl(\Omega^{\bullet_{1}}(\mathscr{G}_{\bullet_{2}}),{\mathsf{d}}^{(\bullet_{1})}_{(\bullet_{2})},\Delta^{(\bullet_{1})}_{(\bullet_{2})}\bigr)\,,

subject to the constraints (
7.1
) and (
7.3
). Such BSS extensions have long been known and studied in the literature in various contexts, see,
e.g.
,
[
Xu04
,
BCWZ04
,
LGX07
,
BC12
,
GSW10
,
Sus12
,
GSW13
,
CS15
,
Sus22
]
.

Definition 7.1
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
C.9
. Let
H\in\Omega^{k+1}(M)
be a de Rham cocycle on the object manifold of a Lie groupoid
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
. A BSS
(k+1)
-cocycle
(H,\rho,0,0,\ldots,0)
with
\rho\in\Omega^{k}(\mathcal{G})
multiplicative shall be called a
multiplicative BSS extension
of
H
. We shall also say, in this case, that
H
is
BSS-extended by

\rho
.

The intimate relation between such BSS extensions and (vertical) vector-bundle morphisms
\mathscr{E}\to{\rm T}^{*}M
with rather tractable equivariance properties with respect to a natural action of (jets of) bisections, which we are about to explore after
[
CS15
]
, shall be seen to play an absolutely crucial rôle in the generalisation of the gauge principle under consideration. This is yet another—this time
a posteriori
—rationale for focusing our attention on them in what follows.

Having fixed the form of the extension of
H_{M}
, co-defining a
\sigma
-model background, we return to the basic question of the reduction of the structure group in the presence of that background. The question may now be rendered more concrete with the help of identity (
7.1
). Indeed, upon pulling back the latter along a candidate rigid-symmetry bisection
\beta\in{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
, we obtain the equality

\displaystyle\bigl(t_{*}\beta\bigr)^{*}H_{M}=H_{M}+{\mathsf{d}}\bigl(\beta^{*}\rho\bigr)\,,

from which the necessary restriction ensues:

\displaystyle\beta^{*}\rho\overset{!}{\in}{\rm ker}\,{\mathsf{d}}\,.

Indeed, for the induced diffeomorphism
t_{*}\beta\in{\rm Diff}(M)
to preserve the holonomy of
\mathcal{G}
(in the definition of the DF amplitude of the PAG
\sigma
-model), it has to map its curvature
H_{M}
to itself under pullback (see: Thm.
D.9
). With hindsight, we impose on
\beta
the stronger condition of
\rho
-holonomicity
(see:
[
CS15
]
):

(7.4)

\displaystyle\beta^{*}\rho\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{=}}0\,,

which is readily seen to ensure—
via
(
7.2
)—the desired prequantisation of the rigid symmetry:

(7.5)

\displaystyle(t_{*}\beta)^{*}\mathcal{G}\equiv\beta^{*}t^{*}\mathcal{G}\cong\beta^{*}s^{*}\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{\beta^{*}\rho}=\mathcal{G}\otimes\mathcal{I}_{0}\equiv\mathcal{G}\,,

see: Def.
5.3
. The above gives rise to the following subgroup of the original structure group.

Proposition/Definition 7.2
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
B.7
and
C.9
. Let
\rho\in\Omega^{k}(\mathscr{G})
be multiplicative. The set

\displaystyle{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G}):=\{\ \beta\in{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})\quad|\quad\beta^{*}\rho=0\ \}

is a subgroup of the group
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
of bisections of
\mathscr{G}
. We shall call it the
\rho
-holonomic group
of
\mathscr{G}
.

Proof.

Let
\beta_{1},\beta_{2}\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
. Then, in virtue of (
7.3
),

\displaystyle(\beta_{1}\cdot\beta_{2})^{*}\rho\equiv\bigl({\rm m}\circ\bigl(\beta_{2}\circ t_{*}\beta_{1},\beta_{1}\bigr)\bigr)^{*}\rho=\bigl(\beta_{2}\circ t_{*}\beta_{1},\beta_{1}\bigr)^{*}\bigl({\rm pr}_{1}^{*}+{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\bigr)\rho=(t_{*}\beta_{1})^{*}\beta_{2}^{*}\rho+\beta_{1}^{*}\rho=0\,,

and so
\beta_{1}\cdot\beta_{2}\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
. Moreover, by the same token,

\displaystyle{\rm Id}^{*}\rho\equiv\bigl({\rm m}\circ({\rm Id},{\rm Id})\bigr)^{*}\rho=({\rm Id},{\rm Id})^{*}\bigl({\rm pr}_{1}^{*}+{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\bigr)\rho=2{\rm Id}^{*}\rho\,,

whence also
{\rm Id}\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
. Finally, using the above, we obtain, for every
\beta\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
,

\displaystyle 0={\rm Id}^{*}\rho\equiv\bigl(\beta^{-1}\cdot\beta\bigr)^{*}\rho=\bigl(t_{*}\beta^{-1}\bigr)^{*}\beta^{*}\rho+\bigl(\beta^{-1}\bigr)^{*}\rho=\bigl(\beta^{-1}\bigr)^{*}\rho\,,

which implies
\beta^{-1}\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
, and completes the proof.
∎

Remark 7.3
.

The rigid-symmetry identity (
7.5
) does not necessitate the stringent condition of
\rho
-holonomicity. Instead, its cohomology variant:

\displaystyle[\beta^{*}\rho]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle!}}{{=}}0\in H^{k}(M)

is sufficient (see: Def.
5.3
). It is clear that the larger set of
weakly
\rho
-holonomic bisections
, which obey this less stringent constraint, also forms a group. Taking into account the increased level of complexity of the analysis of stacky descent—to be carried out in the next section—in this more general case, we restrict our attention to
\rho
-holonomic bisections in what follows. We hope to return to this issue in a future study.

In the prototypical construction of Sec.
6
, the BSS extension is determined by the comomentum, itself derived from the rigid-symmetry analysis and subsequently coupled to the Lie algebra-valued gauge field, under the additional assumption of
{\rm G}
-equivariance. In the present situation, we have to partially reverse this reasoning, and seek to obtain the comomentum with the desired property from the multiplicative 2-form
\rho
. That this is feasible yet far from trivial in the general case is demonstrated in the following remarkable

Theorem 7.4
.

Remark 7.5
.

The statement of the last theorem has been extracted from the constructive proof of the beautiful result
[
CS15
, Thm. 1]
of Crainic, Salazar and Struchiner on the one-to-one correspondence between multiplicative forms and (higher) Spencer operators
12
12

12

The operators generalise, in an appropriate sense, the classical Spencer operators on (first-jet bundles of) vector bundles.
on Lie groupoids (with values in vector-bundle modules of the latter). Crucially, the pair
(\kappa,S)
can be demonstrated to possess further properties, which ensure the independence of presentation (
7.11
) of the arbitrary choice of
j^{1}_{m}\beta
. We choose to omit the discussion of these additional properties for the sake of brevity, but keep in mind the implication emphasised.

Note, in passing, the convenient decomposition

\displaystyle X_{j}={\rm T}_{m}\beta(\underline{X}_{j})+\varepsilon_{j}

of an arbitrary vector
X_{j}\in{\rm T}_{g}\mathscr{G}
used above. It corresponds to the transverse splitting

\displaystyle{\rm T}_{\beta(m)}\mathscr{G}\cong{\rm T}_{m}\beta\bigl({\rm T}_{m}M\bigr)\oplus\bigl({\rm ker}\,{\rm T}s\bigr)_{\beta(m)}

induced by (an arbitrary representative
\beta
of) the first jet
j^{1}_{m}\beta
, in conformity with Prop.
B.15
,

\displaystyle{\rm T}_{m}\beta(\underline{X}_{j})\equiv\chi_{\beta}(X_{j})\,,\qquad\qquad\varepsilon_{j}\equiv\upsilon_{\beta}(X_{j})\,.

Definition 7.6
.

Adopt the notation of Thm.
7.4
. The bundle map

and the map

and—after

]

Now that the (2-)comomentum has been induced from a BSS extension of the curvature of the
\sigma
-model’s gerbe, we may try to imitate the augmentation procedure from Sec.
6
. The success of such an imitation hinges on the concurrence and subtle constructive interplay of three elements:

•

the existence of an
\mathscr{E}
-valued differential form over the spacetime of the field theory transforming in an affine manner under redefinitions of the Lie-groupoidal gauge (in a local presentation as in Cor.
3.12
);

•

the equivariance of the comomentum under the action—defined through a specialisation of Prop.
B.43
—of global bisections representing the redefinitions locally;

•

a reduction of the underlying multiplicative 2-form to an expression fully determined by the comomentum upon restriction to points in the arrow manifold
\mathscr{G}
which belong to the latter bisections (understood as submanifolds diffeomorphically mapped to
M
by
s
and
t
, see: Def.
B.7
).

The first element is straightforward to conceive, at least as long as we stay within a domain
O\subset\Sigma
of trivialisation of the shadow bundle
\mathscr{F}\to\Sigma
, in which we have at our disposal a local gauge field
A\in\Gamma({\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm T}^{*}O\otimes{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\mathscr{E})
, obtained from
\Theta
as in Thm.
3.29
, and exhibiting the desired behaviour, see: Prop.
3.33
. The gauge field may then be coupled to the comomentum through a natural generalisation of Eq. (
6.4
),

(7.13)

\displaystyle\kappa[A]=\kappa\overset{\wedge}{\circ}A+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\left\langle\kappa\circ A\,\overset{\wedge}{,}\,\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ A\right\rangle\,,

in which

•

in the first term:
\kappa
is viewed as a section of
\mathscr{E}^{*}\otimes{\rm T}^{*}M
, the contraction
\circ
refers to the first tensor factor, and the exterior product indicates antisymmetrisation with respect to the second tensor factor, regarded as a direct summand in
{\rm T}^{*}(O\times M)
;

•

in the second term:
\kappa\circ A
is viewed as a section of
{\rm T}^{*}O\otimes{\rm T}^{*}M
, and the exterior product indicates antisymmetrisation with respect to the first tensor factor, regarded as a direct summand in
{\rm T}^{*}(O\times M)
, and present also in
\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ A\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm T}O(\subset{\rm T}(O\times M))\to\mathscr{E}\to{\rm T}M
;

•

the pairing
\left\langle\cdot,\cdot\right\rangle
is that between
{\rm T}^{*}M
(the codomain of
\kappa
) and
{\rm T}M
(the codomain of
\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}
).

Remark 7.7
.

In view of the key rôle played by the 2-forms (

) in the remainder of our discussion, we pause to write out their evaluation on pairs
((v_{1},V_{1}),(v_{2},V_{2}))\in({\rm T}_{\sigma}O\oplus{\rm T}_{m}M)^{\times 2}\equiv{\rm T}_{(\sigma,m)}(O\times M)^{\times 2}
. This is given by the formulæ:

\displaystyle\bigl(\kappa\overset{\wedge}{\circ}A_{i}\bigr)\bigl((v_{1},V_{1}),(v_{2},V_{2})\bigr)=\bigl(\kappa\bigl(A_{i}(v_{2})\bigr)\bigr)(V_{1})-\bigl(\kappa\bigl(A_{i}(v_{1})\bigr)\bigr)(V_{2})\,,

and

\displaystyle\left\langle\kappa\circ A_{i}\,\overset{\wedge}{,}\,\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ A_{i}\right\rangle\bigl((v_{1},V_{1}),(v_{2},V_{2})\bigr)=\bigl(\kappa\bigl(A_{i}(v_{1})\bigr)\bigr)\bigl(\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\bigl(A_{i}(v_{2})\bigr)\bigr)-\bigl(\kappa\bigl(A_{i}(v_{2})\bigr)\bigr)\bigl(\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\bigl(A_{i}(v_{1})\bigr)\bigr)\,.

The second element is captured by the following proposition, in which the naturality of the
\rho
-holonomicity constraint (

) (see: Prop.

) becomes apparent in the light of the

-twisted

-equivariance (

) of the comomentum.

of bisections of the first-jet groupoid
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 12.42015pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-12.42015pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{J^{1}\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 26.64651pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 26.64651pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 26.64651pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
of

along the group homomorphism

of Eq. (

). The restriction of the scalar

-Spencer operator

to

vanishes identically, i.e.,

\displaystyle\forall\ \beta\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})\ \forall\ m\in M\hskip-2.0pt:S\bigl(j^{1}_{m}\beta\bigr)=0\,.

Hence, the

-comomentum
\kappa
is equivariant with respect to the natural action of
{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(J^{1}\mathscr{G})
on the tangent algebroid
\mathscr{E}
of
\mathscr{G}
and the exterior bundle

over its object manifold

.

Proof.

Let
\beta\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
, and

. Upon taking into account the first identity in (

), definition (

) yields the desired result:

(7.14)

\displaystyle S\bigl(j^{1}_{m}\beta\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\rho_{\beta(m)}\circ\wedge^{k}\bigl({\rm T}_{m}\beta\circ\bigl(\widetilde{t}{}_{j^{1}_{m}\beta}\bigr)^{-1}\bigr)=\rho_{\beta(m)}\circ\wedge^{k}\bigl({\rm T}_{m}\beta\circ{\rm T}_{t_{*}\beta(m)}\bigl(t_{*}\beta^{-1}\bigr)\bigr)

(7.16)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\bigl(\beta^{*}\rho\bigr)_{m}\circ\wedge^{k}\bigl({\rm T}_{t_{*}\beta(m)}\bigl(t_{*}\beta^{-1}\bigr)\bigr)=0\,.

Passing to the second statement of the proposition, we note that the two actions to be intertwined by the

-comomentum can be read off from the (commutative) diagram

). The claim now follows directly from (

The final argument in favour of our choice of the reduction scheme comes from the investigation of the third element.

Proposition 7.9
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
7.2
and
7.6
, and of Prop.
B.15
. Let
\rho\in\Omega^{k}(\mathscr{G})
be multiplicative, and let
\kappa
be its
k
-comomentum. Consider an arbitrary
\beta\in{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
, and the splitting
(\chi_{\beta},\upsilon_{\beta})\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm T}_{\beta}\mathscr{G}\equiv{\rm T}\mathscr{G}\big|_{\beta(M)}\cong{\rm T}\beta(M)\oplus{\rm ker}\,{\rm T}s\big|_{\beta(M)}
of
{\rm T}_{\beta}\mathscr{G}
induced by it. The restriction of
\rho
to
{\rm T}_{\beta}\mathscr{G}
is determined by
\kappa
as

(7.18)

\displaystyle\rho\big|_{\beta(M)}=\sum_{p=1}^{k}\,\sum_{\sigma\in{\rm Shuffle}(p,k-p)}\,(-1)^{|\sigma|}\,t^{*}\bigl(\kappa_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{1}\bigr)\bigl(\upsilon_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{2},\upsilon_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{3},\ldots,\upsilon_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{p},\chi_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{p+1},\chi_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{p+2},\ldots,\chi_{\beta}\circ\widehat{\sigma}{}_{k}\bigr)\,,

(7.19)

(7.20)

where

\displaystyle\kappa_{\beta}=\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ\upsilon_{\beta}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm T}_{\beta}\mathscr{G}\longrightarrow\wedge^{k-1}{\rm T}^{*}M\,,

and where we have used the shorthand notation

\displaystyle\widehat{\sigma}{}_{i}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm T}_{\beta}\mathscr{G}^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow{\rm T}_{\beta}\mathscr{G},\ (X_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{k})\longmapsto X_{\sigma(i)}\,,\quad i\in\overline{1,k}\,.

Proof.

The starting point of our discussion is formula (
7.11
), which expresses the multiplicative
k
-form in terms of it Spencer pair
(\kappa,S)
at a
generic
point in
\mathscr{G}
. When putting the formula on the bisection
\beta(M)
, a global choice of a bisection
j^{1}(\beta)
is available such that, at every point
m\in M
, the identity
j^{1}_{m}\beta=j^{1}(\beta)(m)
obtains, which ensures the vanishing of the contribution of the
k
-Spencer operator to
\rho\big|_{\beta(M)}
in virtue of Prop.
7.8
. This settles the question conceptually: The restriction
\rho\big|_{\beta(M)}
is fully determined by the
k
-comomentum
\kappa
. What remains, at this stage, is a direct calculation, in which (
B.19
) is invoked once more (for the aforementioned global choice of the splitting bisection
j^{1}_{\cdot}\beta
) alongside Rem.
7.5
:

(7.22)

\displaystyle\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\bigr)(\varepsilon_{\sigma(1)})\bigl(\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}(\varepsilon_{\sigma(2)}),\ldots,\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}(\varepsilon_{\sigma(p)}),\widetilde{t}{}_{j^{1}_{m}\beta}(\underline{X}_{\sigma(p+1)}),\ldots,\widetilde{t}{}_{j^{1}_{m}\beta}(\underline{X}_{\sigma(k)})\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\bigr)(\varepsilon_{\sigma(1)})\bigl(\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}(\varepsilon_{\sigma(2)}),\ldots,\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}(\varepsilon_{\sigma(p)}),{\rm T}_{m}(t_{*}\beta)(\underline{X}_{\sigma(p+1)}),\ldots,{\rm T}_{m}(t_{*}\beta)(\underline{X}_{\sigma(k)})\bigr)

(7.24)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle t^{*}\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\bigr)(\varepsilon_{\sigma(1)})\bigl(\varepsilon_{\sigma(2)},\ldots,\varepsilon_{\sigma(p)},{\rm T}_{m}\beta(\underline{X}_{\sigma(p+1)}),\ldots,{\rm T}_{m}\beta(\underline{X}_{\sigma(k)})\bigr)

(7.26)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle t^{*}\bigl(\kappa_{\beta}(X_{\sigma(1)})\bigr)\bigl(\upsilon_{\beta}(X_{\sigma(2)}),\ldots,\upsilon_{\beta}(X_{\sigma(p)}),\chi_{\beta}(X_{\sigma(p+1)}),\ldots,\chi_{\beta}(X_{\sigma(k)})\bigr)\,,

and which thus yields the anticipated result.
∎

The foregoing analysis amply demonstrates the functional compatibility of the two assumptions: that of the
\mathscr{G}
-equivariance of the 3-form component
H_{M}
of the tensorial background of the
\sigma
-model, and that of the
\rho
-holonomic reduction of the structure group, and thus emphasises the adequacy of the latter in the present context.

In the next step, we address the issue of the invariance of the metric structure.

Definition 7.10
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
B.7
. Let
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
be a Lie groupoid with a metric object manifold
(M,{\rm g}_{M})
. The
{\rm g}_{M}
-isometric group
of
\mathscr{G}
is the subgroup

\displaystyle{\mathbb{B}}_{{\rm g}_{M}}(\mathscr{G}):=\{\ \beta\in{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})\quad|\quad(t_{*}\beta)^{*}{\rm g}_{M}={\rm g}_{M}\ \}

of the group
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
of (global) bisections of
\mathscr{G}
.

The subtlety concealed by the seemingly benign concept is exposed in

Proposition 7.11
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
7.10
and Ex.
B.21
. Let
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
be a
{\mathbb{B}}
-complete Lie groupoid, in the sense of Def.
B.13
, with a metric object manifold
(M,{\rm g}_{M})
. If
{\mathbb{B}}_{{\rm g}_{M}}(\mathscr{G})={\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
, then all orbits
\mathscr{G}\blacktriangleright m,\ m\in M
of the target action
\blacktriangleright
of
\mathscr{G}
on
M
are zero-dimensional,

\displaystyle\forall\ m\in M\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm dim}(\mathscr{G}\blacktriangleright m)=0\,.

Proof.

Write
[m]\equiv\mathscr{G}\blacktriangleright m
for the sake of brevity. Assume
{\rm dim}\,[m]>0
, and subsequently choose two distinct points
x_{a}\in[m],\ a\in\{1,2\}
alongside the respective non-zero but otherwise
arbitrary
tangent vectors
v_{a}\in{\rm T}_{x_{a}}[m]
. In virtue of Thm.
B.24
, there exists an arrow
g\in\mathscr{G}_{[m]}^{[m]}
and a tangent vector
V\in{\rm T}_{g}\mathscr{G}_{[m]}^{[m]}
with the properties:
(t,s)(g)=(x_{2},x_{1})
and
{\rm T}_{g}(t,s)(V)=(v_{2},v_{1})
. By the assumption of
{\mathbb{B}}
-completeness, we can find
\beta\in{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
such that
\beta(x_{1})=g
, and then also the tangent vector
\xi:={\rm T}_{x_{1}}\beta(v_{1})\in{\rm T}_{g}\beta(M)
such that
{\rm T}_{g}s(\xi)=v_{1}
. We may have
{\rm T}_{g}t(\xi)\neq v_{2}
, but, clearly,
V-\xi\in{\rm T}_{{\rm Id}_{t(g)}}r_{g}(\mathscr{E}_{{\rm Id}_{t(g)}})
, and so—upon recalling Thm.
B.39
—we deform
\beta
within
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
(by flowing it along a suitably chosen compactly supported section of
\mathscr{E}
) to a new bisection
\widetilde{\beta}\in{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
through
\widetilde{\beta}(x_{1})=\beta(x_{1})=g
with
{\rm T}_{g}\widetilde{\beta}(v_{1})=V
(see:
[
Fil25
]
for an explicit construction). We then obtain
v_{2}={\rm T}_{g}t(V)={\rm T}_{g}(t_{*}\widetilde{\beta})(v_{1})
, which contradicts the original assumption about the arbitrariness of the two vectors as it implies that
v_{2}
is an isometric image of
v_{1}
, a property manifestly non-invariant under rescalings.
∎

While certainly very natural from the point of view of the abstract considerations concerning the (homotopy) modelling of the symmetry quotient
M//\mathscr{G}
, our treatment of the topological sector of the
\sigma
-model background has not yet been linked
directly
to rigid symmetries of the field theory under consideration. This last conceptual barrier is overcome in the concluding statement of the present section, in which we also combine the two hitherto independent reduction schemes.

Proposition 7.12
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
5.1
,
7.2
and
7.10
, and of Ex.
B.34
. Let
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
be a Lie groupoid with tangent algebroid
\mathscr{E}
, and let
\rho\in\Omega^{2}(\mathscr{G})
be a multiplicative BSS extension of the de Rham 3-cocycle
H_{M}\in Z^{3}_{\rm dR}(M)
. Consider
\varepsilon\in\Gamma_{\rm c}(\mathscr{E})
. Whenever the flow of the right-invariant vector field
\iota_{\rm R}^{-1}(\varepsilon)\in\Gamma({\rm T}\mathscr{G})_{\rm R}
through the identity bisection
{\rm Id}(M)
remains in

(7.27)

\displaystyle{\mathbb{B}}_{\sigma}(\mathscr{G}):={\mathbb{B}}_{{\rm g}_{M}}(\mathscr{G})\cap{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})\subset{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})

in a parameter (‘time’) range
I_{\delta}\equiv]-\delta,\delta[\subset{\mathbb{R}}
for some
\delta>0
, the corresponding fundamental vector field
\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon\in\Gamma({\rm T}M)
is a tangential rigid symmetry of the
\sigma
-model
\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}
in the sense of Def.
5.3
.

Proof.

The flow
\Phi_{\iota_{\rm R}^{-1}(\varepsilon)}
of the vector field
\iota_{\rm R}^{-1}(\varepsilon)
defines a path

\displaystyle\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\cdot;\cdot):=\Phi_{\iota_{\rm R}^{-1}(\varepsilon)}(\cdot;\cdot)\circ({\rm id}_{\mathbb{R}}\times{\rm Id})\hskip-2.0pt:I_{\delta}\times M\longrightarrow\mathscr{G},\ (\tau,m)\longmapsto\Phi_{\iota_{\rm R}^{-1}(\varepsilon)}\bigl(\tau;{\rm Id}_{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad\Psi_{\varepsilon}\bigl(0;m\bigr)={\rm Id}_{m}

in
{\mathbb{B}}_{\sigma}(\mathscr{G})
(see:
[
CS15
, Rem. 2.11]
), that is,

\displaystyle s\circ\Psi_{\varepsilon}={\rm pr}_{2}\,,

and, for all
\tau\in I_{\delta}
,

\displaystyle\psi[\varepsilon]_{\tau}:=\bigl(t\circ\Psi_{\varepsilon}\bigr)(\tau;\cdot)\in{\rm Isom}(M,{\rm g}_{M})\,,\qquad\qquad\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\tau,\cdot)^{*}\rho=0\,.

We have

\displaystyle\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\tau=0;\cdot)=\varepsilon(\cdot)\,,

and

\displaystyle\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\psi[\varepsilon]_{\tau=0}={\rm T}_{\Phi_{\iota_{\rm R}^{-1}(\varepsilon)}(0;\cdot)}t\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\tau=0;\cdot)\bigr)\equiv\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon(\cdot)\,.

Differentiation of the identity

\displaystyle\psi[\varepsilon]_{\tau}^{*}{\rm g}_{M}={\rm g}_{M}

with respect to time
\tau\in I_{\delta}
at
\tau=0
yields the first anticipated result:

\displaystyle\,{-\hskip-8.0pt\mathscr{L}}_{\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon}{\rm g}_{M}=0\,.

We pull back identity (
7.1
) along the smooth map
\Psi_{\varepsilon}
and evaluate it on a triple
(\partial_{\tau},\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})
of vector fields on its domain
I_{\delta}\times M
, consisting of the global coordinate field
\partial_{\tau}\in\Gamma({\rm T}{\mathbb{R}})
and arbitrary
\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}\in\Gamma({\rm T}M)
(all three being viewed as distinguished sections of
{\rm T}(I_{\delta}\times M)\cong{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}{\rm T}I_{\delta}\oplus{\rm pr}_{2}^{*}{\rm T}M
), to obtain—with the help of Cartan’s formula—the equality

(7.29)

\displaystyle H_{M}\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\psi[\varepsilon],{\rm T}_{2}\psi[\varepsilon](\mathcal{V}_{1}),{\rm T}_{2}\psi[\varepsilon](\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)=H_{M}\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\psi[\varepsilon],{\rm T}_{2}\psi[\varepsilon](\mathcal{V}_{1}),{\rm T}_{2}\psi[\varepsilon](\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)-H_{M}(0,\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl(H_{M}\circ\wedge^{3}{\rm T}(t\circ\Psi_{\varepsilon})\bigr)(\partial_{t},\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})-\bigl(H_{M}\circ\wedge^{3}{\rm T}(s\circ\Psi_{\varepsilon})\bigr)(\partial_{t},\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})={\mathsf{d}}\bigl(\Psi_{\varepsilon}^{*}\rho\bigr)(\partial_{t},\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})

(7.33)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\partial_{\tau}\bigl(\bigl(\rho\circ\wedge^{2}{\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}\bigr)(\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)-\mathcal{V}_{1}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon},{\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)\bigr)+\mathcal{V}_{2}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon},{\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\mathcal{V}_{1})\bigr)\bigr)

\displaystyle-\bigl(\Psi_{\varepsilon}^{*}\rho\bigr)\bigl([\partial_{\tau},\mathcal{V}_{1}],\mathcal{V}_{2}\bigr)+\bigl(\Psi_{\varepsilon}^{*}\rho\bigr)\bigl([\partial_{\tau},\mathcal{V}_{2}],\mathcal{V}_{1}\bigr)-\bigl(\Psi_{\varepsilon}^{*}\rho\bigr)\bigl([\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}],\partial_{\tau}\bigr)

(7.35)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-\mathcal{V}_{1}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon},{\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)\bigr)+\mathcal{V}_{2}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon},{\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}(\mathcal{V}_{1})\bigr)\bigr)-\rho\bigl({\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}\bigl([\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}]\bigr),\tfrac{{\mathsf{d}}\ }{{\mathsf{d}}\tau}\Psi_{\varepsilon}\bigr)\,,

where both
{\rm T}_{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon}
and
{\rm T}_{2}\psi[\varepsilon]
represent derivatives along
M
with the time (
\tau\in I_{\delta}
) held fixed. We may, next, localise the above expression at
\tau=0
, whereby it yields

(7.37)

\displaystyle H_{M}\bigl(\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon,\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}\bigr)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-\mathcal{V}_{1}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\varepsilon,{\rm T}{\rm Id}(\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)\bigr)+\mathcal{V}_{2}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\varepsilon,{\rm T}{\rm Id}(\mathcal{V}_{1})\bigr)\bigr)-\rho\bigl({\rm T}{\rm Id}\bigl([\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}]\bigr),\varepsilon\bigr)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle-\bigl[\mathcal{V}_{1}\bigl({\rm Id}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\varepsilon}\rho\bigr)(\mathcal{V}_{2})\bigr)-\mathcal{V}_{2}\bigl({\rm Id}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\varepsilon}\rho\bigr)(\mathcal{V}_{1})\bigr)-{\rm Id}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\varepsilon}\rho\bigr)\bigl([\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2}]\bigr)\bigr]

(7.39)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-{\mathsf{d}}\bigl({\rm Id}^{*}\bigl(\imath_{\varepsilon}\rho\bigr)\bigr)(\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})\equiv-{\mathsf{d}}\bigl(\kappa(\varepsilon)\bigr)(\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})\,,

see: (
7.6
). Thus, altogether, we obtain the desired result

(7.40)

\displaystyle\imath_{\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon}H_{M}=-{\mathsf{d}}\kappa_{\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon}\,,\qquad\qquad\kappa_{\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\varepsilon}\equiv\kappa(\varepsilon)\,.

∎

Example 7.13
.

The Cartan 3-form
H_{\rm C}
on the object manifold
{\rm G}
of the action groupoid
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G}
from Ex.
5.6
admits a BSS extension
(H_{\rm C},\rho_{\rm AMM},0)
determined by the multiplicative 2-form
\rho_{\rm AMM}\in\Omega^{2}({\rm G}\times{\rm G})
given by

(7.42)

\displaystyle\rho_{\rm AMM}(h,g)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\kappa_{\rm C}(g,t_{a})\wedge\theta_{\rm L}^{a}(h)-\tfrac{1}{2}\,\imath_{\mathcal{K}_{a}(g)}\kappa_{\rm C}(g,t_{b})\,\theta_{\rm L}^{a}(h)\wedge\theta_{\rm L}^{b}(h)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\tfrac{{\mathsf{k}}}{4\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl({\rm T}_{e}{\rm Ad}_{g}\circ\theta_{\rm L}(h)\wedge\theta_{\rm L}(h)+\theta_{\rm L}(h)\wedge\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}(g)+\theta_{\rm R}(g)\bigr)\bigr)\,,\quad(h,g)\in{\rm G}\times{\rm G}

The quadruple
(D({\rm G})\equiv{\rm G}\times{\rm G},\lambda_{\rm AMM},\rho_{\rm AMM},\mu_{\rm AMM})
, with the extra components given by the left action

\displaystyle\lambda_{\rm AMM}\hskip-2.0pt:({\rm G}\times{\rm G})\times D({\rm G})\longrightarrow D({\rm G}),\ \bigl((a,b),(h,g)\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl(a\cdot h\cdot b^{-1},{\rm Ad}_{b}(g)\bigr)\,,

and the map

\displaystyle\mu_{\rm AMM}\hskip-2.0pt:D({\rm G})\longrightarrow{\rm G}\times{\rm G},\ (h,g)\longmapsto\bigl({\rm Ad}_{h}(g),g^{-1}\bigr)\,,

is a prime example of an Alekseev–Malkin–Meinrenken (AMM) quasi-Hamiltonian
{\rm G}\times{\rm G}
-space
[
AMM98
]
. The pair
({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G},(H_{\rm C},\rho_{\rm AMM}))
is referred to as the
AMM groupoid
over
{\rm G}
.

The group
{\rm Bisec}_{\rho_{\rm AMM}}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G})
of
\rho_{\rm AMM}
-holonomic bisections of the AMM groupoid contains a finite subgroup
\iota({\rm G})\subset{\rm Bisec}_{\rho_{\rm AMM}}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G})
given by the image of the homomorphic embedding

\displaystyle\iota\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm G}\longrightarrow{\rm Bisec}_{\rho_{\rm AMM}}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G}),\ h\longmapsto(h,\cdot)\,.

Bisections from
\iota({\rm G})\cong{\rm G}
are also manifestly
{\rm g}_{\rm CK}
-isometric, which puts
\iota({\rm G})
in the rôle of the model of the gauge group of the gauged WZNW
\sigma
-model of
[
GSW11b
,
GSW13
]
.

Remark 7.14
.

It is easy to see that
\iota({\rm G})
is a proper subgroup of
{\rm Bisec}_{\rho_{\rm AMM}}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G})
,

\displaystyle\iota({\rm G})\subsetneq{\rm Bisec}_{\rho_{\rm AMM}}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G})\,.

Indeed, consider the (smooth) diagonal map
\Delta\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm G}\to{\rm G}\times{\rm G},\ g\longmapsto(g,g)
. The map satisfies the identities
s\circ\Delta={\rm id}_{\rm G}
and
t\circ\Delta={\rm id}_{\rm G}\in{\rm Diff}({\rm G})
, and so
\Delta\in{\rm Bisec}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G})\setminus\iota({\rm G})
. It is also trivially
{\rm g}_{\rm CK}
-isometric. In order to see that
\Delta
is
\rho_{\rm AMM}
-holonomic, note that
{\rm T}\Delta=({\rm id}_{{\rm T}{\rm G}},{\rm id}_{{\rm T}{\rm G}})
. Hence,

(7.44)

\displaystyle\Delta^{*}\rho_{\rm AMM}(g)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\tfrac{{\mathsf{k}}}{4\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl({\rm T}_{e}{\rm Ad}_{g}\circ\theta_{\rm L}(g)\wedge\theta_{\rm L}(g)+\theta_{\rm L}(g)\wedge\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}(g)+\theta_{\rm R}(g)\bigr)\bigr)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\tfrac{{\mathsf{k}}}{4\pi}\,{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl(\theta_{\rm L}(g)\wedge\theta_{\rm L}(g)+\theta_{\rm R}(g)\wedge\theta_{\rm L}(g)+\theta_{\rm L}(g)\wedge\theta_{\rm R}(g)\bigr)\,.

However,
{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}(\theta_{\rm H_{1}}\wedge\theta_{\rm H_{2}})=-{\rm tr}_{\mathfrak{g}}(\theta_{\rm H_{2}}\wedge\theta_{\rm H_{1}})
for all
H_{1},H_{2}\in\{{\rm L},{\rm R}\}
, and so—indeed—

\displaystyle\Delta^{*}\rho_{\rm AMM}(g)=0\,,

i.e.,

\displaystyle\Delta\in{\rm Bisec}_{\rho_{\rm AMM}}({\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\rm Ad}{\rm G})\setminus\iota({\rm G})\,.

The tensorial analysis presented in this section provides a stepping stone for the higher-geometric considerations of the next section, ultimately leading to a fully fledged proposal for a gauge principle for the PAG
\sigma
-model with Lie-groupoidal rigid symmetry. We summarise our findings so far in

8.
Gauge descent: Equivariance resp. invariance, augmentation, and stackiness

The conceptual developments and technical results established in the previous section pave the way for a systematic descent of the field theory of interest to the total space of the shadow bundle
\mathscr{F}\to\Sigma
over the theory’s spacetime for an arbitrary symmetry model
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
. The exhaustive treatment of the classic gauging mechanism for group-modelled symmetry reported in
[
GSW10
,
GSW13
,
Sus12
]
and recalled in Sec.
6
provides constructive insight as to how to proceed with the descent in the topologically trivial setting (or locally) in the presence of a multiplicative twist
\rho
in the equivariant structure on the gerbe
\mathcal{G}
of the PAG
\sigma
-model. That said, an important and consequential departure from the very special structure present in the prototypical scenario, reviewed at length in the opening paragraphs of Sec.
7
, is to be noted, to wit: On the total space of a principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}
, there is, in general, no counterpart
13
13

13

Note that, whenever
{\rm dim}\,M>0
, the codomain
{\rm V}\mathscr{P}
of a connection 1-form
\Theta\in\Omega^{1}(\mathscr{P},{\rm V}\mathscr{P})
from Def.
3.22
has a model
{\rm T}\mathscr{G}
of a rank
strictly larger
than that of the corresponding Lie algebroid
\mathscr{E}
(which it contains over the identity bisection).
of the
globally smooth
Lie algebroid-valued 1-form given, in the special case
\mathscr{P}=P\times M
, by the connection 1-form
{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\mathcal{A}\in\Omega^{1}(P\times M)\otimes\mathfrak{g}
. Hence, there is no
direct
lift of the obvious (structurally trivial) Lie-group
oidal
adaptation of the
local
augmentation mechanism (
6.8
) to the total space of the principaloid bundle, which—as emphasised in Sec.
7
—constitutes a natural point of departure for the descent, to the smooth quotient
\mathscr{F}\cong\mathscr{P}/\mathscr{G}
, of the (augmented) pullback
\mu^{*}\mathcal{G}
of the
\sigma
-model gerbe
\mathcal{G}
along the moment map
\mu\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{P}\to M
. Thus, we arrive at the disjunction: Either the multiplicative twist in the latter structure vanishes identically,
\rho\equiv 0
, so that we may try to descend the gerbe along
\mathscr{D}
without involving the gauge field, or we have to work directly with the local augmentations over elements of a trivialising open cover
\mathcal{O}=\{O_{i}\}_{i\in I}
of
\Sigma
, where we have access to local models
O_{i}\times M
of
\mathscr{F}
. As it turns out, the induction of a gerbe on
\mathscr{F}
in
both
cases is governed by the same categorial principle of (2-)stacky descent, originally worked out by Stevenson in his Ph.D. thesis
[
Ste00
]
in direct analogy with Brylinski’s precursor result for principal
{\mathbb{C}}^{\times}
-bundles
[
Bry93
]
. It was subsequently abstracted and elaborated by Nikolaus and Schweigert in
[
NS11
]
. Although its application in the case of an arbitrary twist
\rho
clearly subsumes the non-generic case
\rho=0
, we nevertheless discuss the latter, structurally ‘neater’ scenario, thereby getting an opportunity to employ the said principle in its both (equivalent) formulations: the one for surjective submersions, and the one for open covers.

The fundamental result of gerbe theory—concerning the existence of Breen’s 2-stack structure on gerbes, which largely organises our subsequent considerations—is stated in

Theorem 8.1
.

[
Ste00
]

Given
Y,X\in{\rm{\bf Man}}
, and a surjective submersion
\pi\hskip-2.0pt:Y\twoheadrightarrow X
, there exists a canonical equivalance

\displaystyle\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X)\cong\mathfrak{Desc}(\pi)

between the bicategory of (bundle) gerbes from Thm.
D.5
, and the descent bicategory from Def.
D.11
.

A practical consequence of the above, central to our field-theoretic construction, is extracted in

Corollary 8.2
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.11
and Thm.
D.5
. Every 0-cell
(\mathcal{G},\Phi,\varphi)\in\mathfrak{Desc}(\pi)
canonically induces a gerbe
\underline{\mathcal{G}}\in\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X)
for which there exists a 1-cell

\displaystyle(\Psi,\psi)\hskip-2.0pt:\bigl(\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}},{\rm Id}_{{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}},\lambda_{{\rm Id}_{{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}}}\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\bigl(\mathcal{G},\Phi,\varphi\bigr)

in
\mathfrak{Desc}(\pi)
, written in terms of the left unitor
\lambda_{{\rm Id}_{{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}}}\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm Id}_{{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}}\circ{\rm Id}_{{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}}\xrightarrow{\cong}{\rm Id}_{{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\pi^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}}
of
\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(Y)
.

The principle of (2-)stacky descent reflected in these results finds its most straightforward application in the non-generic situation in which the gerbe of the
\sigma
-model (on
M
) is endowed with an untwisted
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant structure, so that—in particular—its curvature obeys the strong condition
\Delta^{(3)}_{(0)}H_{M}=0
. We then also obtain the identity

\displaystyle{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho=0}(\mathscr{G})\equiv{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})\,,

which reflects the amenability of
all
bisections of the structure groupoid to non-anomalous gauging (in the topological sector). Moreover, the descent passes through the principaloid bundle, as in the prototypical construction of
[
GSW10
]
.

Theorem 8.3

(Unaided gauge descent of gerbes)
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.14
and Prop.
3.13
. Let
\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt
be a Lie groupoid, and let
\mathscr{F}
be the shadow of a principaloid
\mathscr{G}
-bundle
\mathscr{P}
with structure group
{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
. Every
\mathscr{G}
-equivariant gerbe
(\mathcal{G},\Upsilon,\gamma)
canonically induces a gerbe
\underline{\mathcal{G}}\in\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(\mathscr{F})
with the following property

(8.1)

\displaystyle\forall\ \Phi\in{\rm Gauge}(\mathscr{P})\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{F}_{*}(\Phi)^{*}\underline{\mathcal{G}}\cong\underline{\mathcal{G}}\,.

Proof.

The theorem is a simple corollary to the more general Thm.
8.6
, which shall be stated and proven presently. Therefore, here, we restrict to laying out the logic of the present proof, which is—essentially—that of (the proof of)
[
GSW10
, Thm. 5.9]
, and, as such, is largely independent of that of the constructive proof of the general theorem.

In virtue of Prop.
C.7
, the principality of the defining action
\varrho
of the structure groupoid
\mathscr{G}
on
\mathscr{P}
and the submersive surjectivity of the moment map
\mu\hskip-2.0pt:\mathscr{P}\to M
imply the existence of the simplicial epimorphism
\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}
as in (
C.16
). The pullback of
(\mathscr{G},\Upsilon,\gamma)
along this epimorphism yields a descent datum

\displaystyle\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}(\mathcal{G},\Upsilon,\gamma)\equiv\bigl(\mu^{*}\mathcal{G},\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}\Upsilon,(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1,2},\phi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{2,3})^{*}\gamma\bigr)\in{\mathfrak{D}esc}(\mathscr{D})\,.

This is so due to the strict 2-functoriality of pullback (see:
[
Wal07b
]
), which implies

\displaystyle\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}\Upsilon\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm pr}_{1}^{*}\bigl(\mu^{*}\mathcal{G}\bigr)=\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}t^{*}\mathcal{G}\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}s^{*}\mathcal{G}={\rm pr}_{2}^{*}\bigl(\mu^{*}\mathcal{G}\bigr)\,,

and

\displaystyle(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1,2},\phi_{\mathscr{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{2,3})^{*}\gamma\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm pr}_{2,3}^{*}\bigl(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}\Upsilon\bigr)\circ{\rm pr}_{1,2}^{*}\bigl(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}\Upsilon\bigr){\mathrel{\to}^{\ \cong\ }}{\rm pr}_{1,3}^{*}\bigl(\phi_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}\Upsilon\bigr)\,,

the latter 2-isomorphism inheriting coherence from
\gamma
. Above, we have used the simpliciality of
\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}
. The descent datum induces a gerbe
\underline{\mathscr{G}}\in\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(\mathscr{F})
by Thm.
8.2
.

The gauge invariance of the induced gerbe
\underline{\mathscr{G}}
can now be proven along the lines of (the proof of)
[
GSW10
, Thm. 5.9]
, given for the case of the action groupoid
{\rm G}\,{\hskip-1.13791pt\ltimes\hskip-1.42271pt}_{\lambda}M
: In consequence of the
\mathscr{G}
-equivariance of
\Phi
, the existence of the 1-isomorphism (
8.1
) is ensured by that of an isomorphism

\displaystyle\Phi_{\bullet}^{*}\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}(\mathcal{G},\Upsilon,\gamma)\cong\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}(\mathcal{G},\Upsilon,\gamma)\,,

in which
\Phi_{\bullet}^{*}
represents a natural simplicial lift of
\Phi^{*}
, with components
\Phi^{*}_{n}=(\Phi^{\times n+1})^{*}
. The meaningfulness of its application to the simplicial extension
\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}^{*}(\mathcal{G},\Upsilon,\gamma)
hinges, once more, on the strict 2-functoriality of pullback.

That the desired isomorphism (or, indeed, an equality) exists now follows from the
\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}
-invariance of the simplicial extension
\varepsilon_{\mathscr{P}}
of the manifestly
\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}
-invariant moment map
\mu
(see: Thm.
3.8
). This ultimately stems from the
\lambda_{\mathscr{P}}
-invariance of the division map
\phi_{\mathscr{P}}
of the principaloid bundle, which is readily demonstrated in its local presentation (
3.8
) (see: Cor.
3.12
).
∎

In the presence of a non-vanishing twist,
\rho\neq 0
, the mechanism sketched above breaks down, and we need to couple the gerbe to the gauge field provided by the principaloid bundle
\mathscr{P}
in order to remove the obstruction to its descent to
\mathscr{F}
. The stage for the connection-aided gauging of the gerbe’s character is set in

Definition 8.4
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
3.28
,
7.2
and
7.6
, and of Thm.

. Let

Thus, through a subtle interplay between the affine transformation law for the
\mathscr{E}
-valued local gauge field on the principaloid bundle over the spacetime of the
\sigma
-model with an intrinsic bicategorial symmetry property of its gerbe—namely, its
\rho
-twisted equivariance—and the corresponding (
\rho
-holonomic) reduction of the group of diffeomorphisms, which ensures coherent preservation of the class of the gerbe in its presence and (restricted) equivariance of the induced comomentum map, we arrive at a definition of a gerbe over the configuration bundle of the
\sigma
-model with the groupoidal symmetry (implemented by)
{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})
gauged. This is, clearly, a tightly knit geometric structure, whose naturality and indispensability in the present context is further corroborated and amplified by a refinement of Thm.
7.4
, also due to Crainic
et al.
(see:
[

, Cor. 3.18]
, but also
[
BCWZ04
, Thm. 2.5]
), which establishes a one-to-one correspondence between multiplicative forms and their comomenta on source-simply connected Lie groupoids. Such groupoids are, in turn, uniquely associated with the underlying (integrable) Lie algebroids
\mathscr{E}
in virtue of Lie’s First Theorem for Lie algebroids as the corresponding
monodromy groupoids
(see:
[
MM02
, Prop. 3.3]
, and also
[
CLF03
]
), and so are, in particular, natural integrated/large-symmetry models for field theories with Lie-algebroidal tangential symmetries (as,
e.g.
, the Poisson
\sigma
-model of
[

,
SS94
]
). We shall invoke Thm.

in the formulation of the fully fledged gauged PAG
\sigma
-model in Sec.
10
, after an in-depth analysis—carried out in the next section—of the cohomology behind the gauge principle emerging from our considerations.
