) submerses
M
as

\displaystyle\check{\pi}\hskip-2.0pt:\check{Y}_{\mathcal{O}}\twoheadrightarrow M\,,\ (x,i)\longmapsto x\,.

The nerve
N_{\bullet}({\rm Pair}_{\check{\pi}}(\check{Y}{}_{\mathcal{O}}))\equiv N_{\bullet}\mathcal{O}
of the submersion groupoid
{\rm Pair}_{\check{\pi}}(\check{Y}{}_{\mathcal{O}})
(see: Ex.
B.4
), with

, where
O_{i_{0}i_{1}\cdots i_{n}}\equiv O_{i_{0}}\cap O_{i_{1}}\cap\cdots\cap O_{i_{n}}
, is termed the
Čech nerve
of
\mathcal{O}
. The corresponding Dupont operators are known as the
Čech coboundary operators
.

Proposition C.7

\displaystyle\varepsilon_{\rm\breve{P}}\hskip-2.0pt:N_{\bullet}\bigl({\rm Pair}_{\pi_{\rm\breve{P}}}({\rm\breve{P}})\bigr)\twoheadrightarrow N_{\bullet}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.55554pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.55554pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)\,.

Proof.

The principality of
\varrho
can equivalently be understood as the isomorphy of the groupoids
19
19

19

The appearance of the opposite groupoid in the codomain is intuitively clear: It is ultimately encoded in the following identities
(s\circ\imath_{1})(p_{2},p_{1})\equiv{\rm pr}_{1}(p_{2},\phi_{\rm\breve{P}}(p_{2},p_{1}))=p_{2}\equiv\widetilde{t}(p_{2},p_{1})
and
(t\circ\imath_{1})(p_{2},p_{1})\equiv\varrho(p_{2},\phi_{\rm\breve{P}}(p_{2},p_{1}))=p_{1}\equiv\widetilde{s}(p_{2},p_{1})
.

\displaystyle\imath\hskip-2.0pt:{\rm Pair}_{\pi_{\rm\breve{P}}}({\rm\breve{P}})\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\bigl({\rm\breve{P}}\rtimes\mathscr{G}\bigr)^{\rm op}\,,

with the object component of
\imath
given by
\imath_{0}={\rm id}_{{\rm\breve{P}}}
, and the morphism component induced from
\phi_{\rm\breve{P}}
as

\displaystyle\imath_{1}=({\rm pr}_{1},\phi_{\rm\breve{P}})\equiv({\rm pr}_{1},\varrho)^{-1}\,.

The above implies the existence of a simplicial extension

\displaystyle\widetilde{\imath}\hskip-2.0pt:N_{\bullet}\bigl({\rm Pair}_{\pi_{\rm\breve{P}}}({\rm\breve{P}})\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }N_{\bullet}\bigl(\bigl({\rm\breve{P}}\rtimes\mathscr{G}\bigr)^{\rm op}\bigr)\,,\qquad\bigl(\widetilde{\imath}{}_{0},\widetilde{\imath}{}_{1}\bigr)\equiv\imath\,.

Explicitly, we find

(C.18)

\displaystyle\widetilde{\imath}{}_{n}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl(\imath_{1}\times{\rm id}_{\mathscr{G}^{\times n-1}}\bigr)\circ\bigl({\rm id}_{\rm\breve{P}}\times\imath_{1}\times{\rm id}_{\mathscr{G}^{\times n-2}}\bigr)\circ\cdots\circ\bigl({\rm id}_{{\rm\breve{P}}^{\times n-2}}\times\imath_{1}\times{\rm id}_{\mathscr{G}}\bigr)\circ\bigl({\rm id}_{{\rm\breve{P}}^{\times n-1}}\times\imath_{1}\bigr)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\bigl({\rm pr}_{1},\phi_{\rm\breve{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{1,2},\phi_{\rm\breve{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{2,3},\ldots,\phi_{\rm\breve{P}}\circ{\rm pr}_{n,n+1}\bigr)

in the convenient presentation

\displaystyle N_{n}\bigl(\bigl({\rm\breve{P}}\rtimes\mathscr{G}\bigr)^{\rm op}\bigr)={\rm\breve{P}}\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{t\circ{\rm pr}_{1}}\hskip-2.0pt\mathscr{G}_{n}\equiv{\rm\breve{P}}\hskip-2.0pt{}_{\mu}\hskip-3.0pt\times_{t\circ{\rm pr}_{1}}\hskip-2.0ptN_{n}\bigl(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt\bigr)\,,\quad n\in{\mathbb{N}}^{\times}\,,

In the latter, we have the surjective submersions

\displaystyle\mu_{n}:={\rm pr}_{2,3,\ldots,n+1}\hskip-2.0pt:N_{n}\bigl(\bigl({\rm\breve{P}}\rtimes\mathscr{G}\bigr)^{\rm op}\bigr)\twoheadrightarrow N_{n}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)\,,

which combine with the surjective submersion

\displaystyle\mu_{0}:=\mu\hskip-2.0pt:N_{0}\bigl(\bigl({\rm\breve{P}}\rtimes\mathscr{G}\bigr)^{\rm op}\bigr)\equiv{\rm\breve{P}}\twoheadrightarrow M\equiv N_{0}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)

to yield a simplicial epimorphism

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu}\ :\ N_{\bullet}\bigl(\bigl({\rm\breve{P}}\rtimes_{\varrho}\mathscr{G}\bigr)^{\rm op}\bigr)\twoheadrightarrow N_{\bullet}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)\,.

Altogether, then, we arrive at the sought-after simplicial epimorphism

\displaystyle\varepsilon_{\rm\breve{P}}:=\widetilde{\mu}\circ\widetilde{\imath}\hskip-2.0pt:N_{\bullet}\bigl({\rm Pair}_{\pi_{\rm\breve{P}}}({\rm\breve{P}})\bigr)\twoheadrightarrow N_{\bullet}(\hskip-5.0pt\begin{aligned} \lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 6.92361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-6.92361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\mathscr{G}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise-1.07639pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 21.14998pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{M}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces\end{aligned}\hskip-3.0pt)\,.

Definition C.10
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
C.3
. Let
M_{\bullet}\hskip-2.0pt:\triangle^{\rm op}\to{\rm{\bf Man}}
be a simplicial manifold with face maps
\{d^{(n+1)}_{i}\ |\ i\in\overline{0,n}\}_{n\in{\mathbb{N}}}
. A family
\{\mathcal{O}_{M_{n}}\}_{n\in{\mathbb{N}}}
of open covers
\mathcal{O}_{M_{n}}=\{O^{(n)}_{i_{n}}\}_{i_{n}\in I_{n}}
of the respective objects
M_{n}\in{\rm{\bf Man}}
is called
simplicial
if the index sets
I_{n},\ n\in{\mathbb{N}}
compose a simplicial set
I_{\bullet}\hskip-2.0pt:\triangle^{\rm op}\to{\rm{\bf Set}}
with face maps
\iota^{(n+1)}_{i}\equiv I_{\bullet}(\delta^{(n+1)}_{i})\hskip-2.0pt:I_{n+1}\to I_{n}
such that the relation

\displaystyle d^{(n+1)}_{j}\bigl(O^{(n+1)}_{i_{n}}\bigr)\subset O^{(n)}_{\iota^{(n+1)}_{j}(i_{n})}

holds true for all
j\in\overline{0,n+1}
and
n\in{\mathbb{N}}^{\times}
.

.

Tu06

For every simplicial manifold, and every collection of open covers of its objects, there exists a refinement of the latter which is simplicial in the sense of Def.

Appendix D
Gerbes, characters, equivariance and descent

\displaystyle\check{C}^{0}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\underline{\Omega^{2}}\bigr)\oplus\check{C}^{1}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\underline{\Omega^{1}}\bigr)\oplus\check{C}^{2}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\underline{{\rm U}(1)}\bigr)

(D.6)

\displaystyle A^{3}(\mathcal{O})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\check{C}^{1}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\underline{\Omega^{2}}\bigr)\oplus\check{C}^{2}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\underline{\Omega^{1}}\bigr)\oplus\check{C}^{3}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\underline{{\rm U}(1)}\bigr)\qquad\ldots

and the
Deligne differentials

\displaystyle D^{(0)}(f_{i})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl(-{\mathsf{i}}\,f_{i}^{-1}\,{\mathsf{d}}f_{i},f_{j}^{-1}\cdot f_{i}\big|_{O_{ij}}\bigr)

(D.8)

\displaystyle D^{(1)}(\Pi_{i},\chi_{ij})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl({\mathsf{d}}\Pi_{i},-{\mathsf{i}}\,\chi_{ij}^{-1}\,{\mathsf{d}}\chi_{ij}+(\Pi_{j}-\Pi_{i})\big|_{O_{ij}},\chi_{jk}^{-1}\cdot\chi_{ik}\cdot\chi_{ij}^{-1}\big|_{O_{ijk}}\bigr)

(D.10)

\displaystyle D^{(2)}(B_{i},A_{ij},g_{ijk})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl({\mathsf{d}}A_{ij}-(B_{j}-B_{i})\big|_{O_{ij}},-{\mathsf{i}}\,g_{ijk}^{-1}\,{\mathsf{d}}g_{ijk}+(A_{jk}-A_{ik}+A_{ij})\big|_{O_{ijk}},g_{jkl}^{-1}\cdot g_{ikl}\cdot g_{ijl}^{-1}\cdot g_{ijk}\big|_{O_{ijkl}}\bigr)

(D.12)

\displaystyle{\it etc.}

Its cohomology

\displaystyle{\mathbb{H}}^{\bullet}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\mathscr{D}^{\bullet}(2;X)\bigr)\equiv H^{\bullet}\bigl(A^{\bullet}(\mathcal{O}),D^{(\bullet)}\bigr)

is termed the (
real
)
degree-2 Beilinson–Deligne cohomology
of
X
associated to
\mathcal{O}
. Under refinement of the cover (i.e., for
\mathcal{O}
sufficiently fine—e.g., good), it yields the (
real
)
degree-2 Beilinson–Deligne cohomology
of
X

\displaystyle{\mathbb{H}}^{\bullet}\bigl(X,\mathscr{D}^{\bullet}(2;X)\bigr)=\underset{\scriptsize{\mathcal{O}}}{\varinjlim}\,{\mathbb{H}}^{\bullet}\bigl(\mathcal{O},\mathscr{D}^{\bullet}(2;X)\bigr)

Proposition D.2
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.1
. There exist canonical isomorphisms

\displaystyle{\mathbb{H}}^{0}\bigl(X,\mathscr{D}^{\bullet}(2;X)\bigr)\cong H^{0}\bigl(X,{\rm U}(1)\bigr)\,,\qquad\qquad{\mathbb{H}}^{1}\bigl(X,\mathscr{D}^{\bullet}(2;X)\bigr)\cong H^{1}\bigl(X,{\rm U}(1)\bigr)\,.

.

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.1
. Every class

given by

\displaystyle\mathcal{W}^{3}(X;0)\times\mathcal{W}^{3}(X;H)\longrightarrow\mathcal{W}^{3}(X;H)

(D.13)

(D.14)

\displaystyle\bigl([(\beta_{i},\alpha_{ij},\gamma_{ijk})],[(B_{i},A_{ij},g_{ijk})]\bigr)\longmapsto[(B_{i}+\beta_{i},A_{ij}+\alpha_{ij},g_{ijk}\cdot\gamma_{ijk})]\,.

There is a canonical isomorphism

\displaystyle\mathcal{W}^{3}(X;0)\cong H^{2}\bigl(X,{\rm U}(1)\bigr)\,.

Theorem D.5
.

[
Ste00
,
Wal07b
]

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.4
. Gerbes over a given base
X\in{\rm{\bf Man}}
, together with gerbe 1-isomorphisms between them, and gerbe 2-isomorphisms between the latter, form a monoidal bicategory
\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X)
(in the sense of
[
Bén68
]
) with duality. Moreover, every smooth map
f\in C^{\infty}(X_{1},X_{2})
canonically induces a (strict monoidal) 2-functor
f^{*}\hskip-2.0pt:\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X_{2})\to\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X_{1})
.

Proposition D.6
.

Adopt the notation of Defs.
D.1
and
D.4
, and of Thm.
D.3
. There is a one-to-one correspondence between 1-isomorphism classes of gerbes over
X
and classes in
{\mathbb{H}}^{2}(X,\mathscr{D}^{\bullet}(2;X))
. Under this correspondence, 1-isomorphism classes of gerbes of curvature
H
are identified with elements in
\mathcal{W}^{3}(X;H)
. In particular, such gerbes are classified by the cohomology group
H^{2}(X,{\rm U}(1))
.

Proposition D.7
.

Adopt the notation of Def.
D.1
. Let the 2-cocycles
b_{a}\in{\rm ker}\,D^{(2)},\ a\in\{1,2\}
represent the respective gerbes
\mathcal{G}_{a}\in\mathfrak{BGrb}_{\nabla}(X)
under the correspondence from Prop.
D.6
. A 1-isomorphism
\Phi\hskip-2.0pt:\mathcal{G}_{1}\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{G}_{2}
is then represented by a 1-cochain
p\in A^{1}(\mathcal{O})
such that

\displaystyle b_{2}=b_{1}+D^{(1)}p\,,

and a 2-isomorphism
\varphi\hskip-2.0pt:\Phi_{1}\overset{\cong}{\Rightarrow}\Phi_{2}
between two such 1-isomorphisms
\Phi_{b}\hskip-2.0pt:\mathcal{G}_{1}\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{G}_{2},\ b\in\{1,2\}
, given by the respective 1-cochains
p_{b}\in A^{1}(\mathcal{O})
, is represented by a 0-cochain
f\in A^{0}(\mathcal{O})
such that

\displaystyle p_{2}=p_{1}+D^{(0)}f\,.

Accordingly, 2-isomorphism classes of 1-isomorphisms between given gerbes
\mathcal{G}_{a},\ a\in\{1,2\}
are classified by the cohomology group
H^{1}(X,{\rm U}(1))
.

Appendix E
A proof of Theorem
8.6
.

Throughout this appendix, we assume the
reduced
form of the transition 1-cocycle:
\beta_{ij}\hskip-2.0pt:O_{ij}\to{\mathbb{B}}_{\rho}(\mathscr{G})\subset{\mathbb{B}}(\mathscr{G})
, and consider smooth maps

from (
3.36
), alongside diffeomorphisms

\displaystyle B_{ij}:=\mathscr{F}\tau_{i}\circ\mathscr{F}\tau_{j}^{-1}\big|_{O_{ij}\times M}\equiv\bigl({\rm pr}_{1},t\circ\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}\bigr)\hskip-2.0pt:O_{ij}\times M\longrightarrow O_{ij}\times M,\ (\sigma,m)\longmapsto\bigl(\sigma,t_{*}\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)(m)\bigr)\,.

The latter satisfy the obvious gluing identities

which reflect the 1-cocycle identities (
3.3
).

Lemma E.1
.

The curvings
\kappa[A_{i}]
from Eq. (
8.2
) satisfy the identities

(E.1)

\displaystyle\kappa[A_{j}]\big|_{O_{ij}\times M}-B_{ij}^{*}\kappa[A_{i}]\big|_{O_{ij}\times M}=\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}^{*}\rho\,.

Proof of Lemma:

At a given point
(\sigma,m)\in O_{ij}\times M
, the pullback

\displaystyle\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}^{*}\rho(\sigma,m)\equiv\rho\circ\wedge{}^{2}{\rm T}_{(\sigma,m)}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}

localises the multiplicative 2-form
\rho
on the bisection
\beta_{ij}(\sigma)(M)\subset\mathscr{G}
, and so we may invoke Prop.
7.9
. The relevant splitting (see: Prop.
B.15
) is engendered by the decomposition

\displaystyle{\rm T}_{(\sigma,m)}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}={\rm T}_{m}\bigl(\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)+{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\,,

with
{\rm im}\,{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\subset({\rm ker}\,{\rm T}s)_{\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\sigma,m)}
. Here, it is to be understood that
{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)
(resp.
{\rm T}_{m}(\beta_{ij}(\sigma))
) acts on the first (resp. the second) summand in
{\rm T}_{\sigma}O_{ij}\oplus{\rm T}_{m}M\equiv{\rm T}_{(\sigma,m)}(O_{ij}\times M)
. Hence, identity (
7.20
) takes the form

(E.5)

\displaystyle\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}^{*}\rho(\sigma,m)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\bigr)\bigl({\rm T}_{m}\bigl(t_{*}\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)

\displaystyle-\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)\bigl({\rm T}_{m}\bigl(t_{*}\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\bigr)

\displaystyle+\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\bigr)\bigl({\rm T}_{\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\sigma,m)}t\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)

(E.11)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\bigr)\bigl({\rm T}_{m}\bigl(t_{*}\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)

\displaystyle-\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)\bigl({\rm T}_{m}\bigl(t_{*}\beta_{ij}(\sigma)\bigr)\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\bigr)

\displaystyle+\bigl(\kappa\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{1}\bigr)\bigl(\alpha_{\mathscr{E}}\circ\theta_{\rm R}\circ{\rm T}_{\sigma}\widetilde{\beta}{}_{ij}(\cdot,m)\circ{\rm pr}_{2}\bigr)\,,
